title: حِكَايَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ
titleEn: The Tailor's Tale, continued: the Barber's Brothers — the Blind Man, the Butcher and the Glass-Seller
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 258–266 (Night 32, continuing directly from nights-31), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 32 continues the barber's account of his six brothers to the Caliph. The second brother's humiliation ends with his being flogged by the tanners of Baghdad and banished; the third, Faqīq, a blind man, is led up to a rooftop by a householder and then, followed home by that man, is beaten with his fellow beggars before the governor when the stranger feigns blindness and steals a share of their money. The fourth, a one-eyed butcher, is cheated with counterfeit silver by a sinister old man, who then shows a slaughtered man hanging in his shop; later a king who cannot bear the sight of a one-eyed man has him beaten, and he is flogged again as a burglar. The fifth, a cropped-eared beggar, buys glassware with his inheritance and, sitting against a wall, daydreams of marrying the vizier's daughter; the night ends mid-dream as Shahrazad falls silent. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some of the Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاكَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالثَّلٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā-kānat al-laylatu al-thāniyatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the second-and-thirtieth.
sentences.i: And when the thirty-second night came,
sentences.n: The night-opening formula. The print joins فلماكانت into one word, and writes الثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون, so it is pointed with a dagger alif (ٰ) to read thalāthūn.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ أَخٰ الْمُزَيِّنِ لَمَّا قَالَتْ لَهُ الْعَجُوزُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna akhā al-muzayyini lammā qālat lahu al-ʿajūzu
sentences.l: She said: It-reached me, O king the-fortunate, that the brother of-the-barber, when said to-him the old-woman:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the old woman said to the barber's brother,
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and أن together as one word, السعيدان; read it as السَّعِيدَ أَنَّ, "the fortunate, that". اخ is printed without the final alif of أخا, which the accusative after أَنَّ would need; it is pointed with a dagger alif (ٰ). The brother is the barber's own, whose adventure with the old woman and the girl was begun the night before.

sentences.t: اِقْلَعْ ثِيَابَكَ
sentences.tr: iqlaʿ thiyābaka
sentences.l: Pull-off your-clothes.
sentences.i: "Take off your clothes."

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَهُوَ غَائِبٌ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ فَقَلَعَ ثِيَابَهُ وَبَقِيَ عُرْيَانًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-huwa ghāʾibun ʿani al-wujūdi fa-qalaʿa thiyābahu wa-baqiya ʿuryānan
sentences.l: And he-rose, and he (was) absent from the-existence; and he-pulled-off his-clothes and remained naked.
sentences.i: So he got up, utterly lost to the world, took off his clothes, and stood there naked.
sentences.n: غَائِبٌ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ, "absent from existence", is the usual idiom for someone dazed or beside himself, here with desire.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ لِأَخِي قُمِ الْآنَ وَاجْرِ وَأَجْرِي أَنَا أَيْضًا
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-jāriyatu li-akhī qumi al-āna wa-ijri wa-ajrī anā aydan
sentences.l: And said the girl to-my-brother: Rise now and run, and I-run, I, also.
sentences.i: Then the girl said to my brother, "Get up now and run, and I will run too."
sentences.n: The narrator is now the barber himself, telling of his brother, hence لِأَخِي "to my brother" (the quoted tale began last night with Shahrazād's own voice). وَاجْرِ is the imperative "and run"; the second verb وَأَجْرِي is first person, "and I run", an indicative where Classical would put the subjunctive after an imperative.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَعَرَّتْ هِيَ أَيْضًا
sentences.tr: thumma taʿarrat hiya aydan
sentences.l: Then she-stripped, she, also.
sentences.i: Then she stripped as well.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ إِنْ أَرَدْتَ شَيْأً اتَّبِعْنِي
sentences.tr: qālat lahu in aradta shayʾan ittabiʿnī
sentences.l: She-said to-him: If you-wished a-thing, follow-me.
sentences.i: She said to him, "If you want something, follow me."
sentences.n: شَيْأً "a thing, something": the print already writes the hamza (precomposed أ) and the tanwīn here; we add only the sukūn. The girl's "something" is a sly euphemism, as what follows makes plain.

sentences.t: فَجَرَتْ قُدَّامَهُ فَتَبِعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-jarat quddāmahu fa-tabiʿahā
sentences.l: And she-ran in-front-of-him, and he-followed-her.
sentences.i: She ran ahead of him, and he followed her.
sentences.n: قُدَّام, "in front of", is the colloquial form; Classical prefers أَمَامَ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَعَلَتْ تَدْخُلُ مِنْ مَحَلٍّ إِلَى مَحَلٍّ وَتَخْرُجُ إِلَى الْآخَرِ وَأَخِي وَرَاءَهَا وَقَدْ غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ الشَّوْقُ وَزُبُّهُ قَائِمٌ كَأَنَّهُ مَجْنُونٌ
sentences.tr: thumma jaʿalat tadkhulu min maḥallin ilā maḥallin wa-takhruju ilā al-ākhari wa-akhī warāʾahā wa-qad ghalaba ʿalayhi al-shawqu wa-zubbuhu qāʾimun ka-annahu majnūnun
sentences.l: Then she-began (to) enter from a-place to a-place, and go-out to the-other, and my-brother behind-her, and had overcome upon-him the-longing, and his-penis (was) standing, as-though-he (were) a-madman.
sentences.i: Then she began to go in from one place to another and out into yet another, with my brother behind her, overcome with desire, his penis standing up as if he were mad.
sentences.n: جَعَلَ followed by an imperfect verb means "began to". مَحَلّ is a "place" or "spot" (the girl leads him through rooms and passages). The print marks زُبّه with damma and shadda; we keep those marks and supply the rest. زُبّ is a blunt word for the penis, as is الأير below. A bare noun or participle after وَ (وَزُبُّهُ قَائِمٌ) is a circumstantial clause, "with his member standing".

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَتْ هِيَ قُدَّامَهُ فِي مَكَانٍ مُظْلِمٍ فَدَخَلَ أَخِي أَيْضًا وَهُوَ يَجْرِي وَرَاءَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-dakhalat hiya quddāmahu fī makānin muẓlimin fa-dakhala akhī aydan wa-huwa yajrī warāʾahā
sentences.l: And she-entered, she, in-front-of-him into a-place dark; and entered my-brother also, and he running behind-her.
sentences.i: She went in ahead of him into a dark place, and my brother went in too, running after her.

sentences.t: فَدَاسَ مَوْضِعًا رَقِيقًا فَانْخَسَفَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-dāsa mawḍiʿan raqīqan fa-inkhasafa bihi
sentences.l: And he-trod (on) a-spot thin, and it-gave-way with-him.
sentences.i: He stepped on a thin spot in the floor, and it gave way under him.
sentences.n: اِنْخَسَفَ is "to cave in, collapse"; بِهِ "with him" means that it collapsed taking him along. رَقِيق is "thin, flimsy".

sentences.t: فَلَا دَرَي بِنَفْسِهِ إِلَّا وَهُوَ فِي وَسَطِ الزُّقَاقِ وَهُوَ فِي سُوقِ الْجَلَّادِينَ وَهُمْ يُنَادُونَ عَلَى الْجُلُودِ وَيَشْتَرُونَ وَيَبِيعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lā darā bi-nafsihi illā wa-huwa fī wasaṭi al-zuqāqi wa-huwa fī sūqi al-jallādīna wa-hum yunādūna ʿalā al-julūdi wa-yashtarūna wa-yabīʿūna
sentences.l: And not he-knew of-himself, except (that) he (was) in the-middle of-the-alley, and he (was) in the-market of-the-hide-dealers, and they calling upon the-hides and buying and selling.
sentences.i: The next thing he knew, he was in the middle of an alley, in the market of the hide-dealers, where they were crying their hides for sale and buying and selling.
sentences.n: The print has فلا دري with a space, and دري with yā for the final alif (the edition often writes ى as ي). It reads دَرَى, "he knew"; the negative is لَا with a perfect verb, a Middle Arabic way of saying "he did not know" (Classical would use لَمْ يَدْرِ). The phrase لَا دَرَى بِنَفْسِهِ ... إِلَّا وَهُوَ means "he came to himself only to find that he was ...". الْجَلَّادِين are dealers in skins and hides (جِلْد, "hide"); the word can also mean "floggers", which makes the sequel apt. نَادَى عَلَى is "to cry (wares) for sale".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ وَهُوَ عُرْيَانٌ قَائِمُ الْأَيْرِ مَحْلُوقُ اللِّحَيْنِ وَ الْحَوَاجِبِ مُحْمَرُّ الْوَجْهِ صَاحُوا عَلَيْهِ وَصَفَّقُوا عَلَيْهِ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾawhu ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati wa-huwa ʿuryānun qāʾimu al-ayri maḥlūqu al-liḥayni wa-al-ḥawājibi muḥmarru al-wajhi ṣāḥū ʿalayhi wa-ṣaffaqū ʿalayhi bi-aydīhim
sentences.l: And when they-saw-him upon that state, and he (was) naked, standing (of) the-penis, shaven (of) the-two-beards and the-eyebrows, reddened (of) the-face, they-shouted at-him and clapped at-him with-their-hands.
sentences.i: When they saw him in that state, naked, his penis erect, his beard and eyebrows shaved off, his face red, they shouted at him and clapped their hands at him.
sentences.n: The print has اللحين, with a single yā, and then a separate و before الحواجب. I read it as the dual اللِّحَيْن "the two sides of the beard" (the cheeks and jaw); it may instead be a misprint for اللحية "the beard". The unusual spacing وَ الْحَوَاجِبِ is the print's. The series قَائِمُ ... مَحْلُوقُ ... مُحْمَرُّ is a run of "state" phrases; each is an annexation ("standing of penis") in the manner of Arabic descriptive idiom. بِأَيْدِيهِمْ: بِـ marks the instrument.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلُوا يَضْرِبُونَهُ بِالْجُلُودِ وَهُوَ عُرْيَانٌ حَتَّى غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿalū yaḍribūnahu bi-al-julūdi wa-huwa ʿuryānun ḥattā ghushiya ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And they-began (to) strike-him with-the-hides, and he (was) naked, until it-was-covered over-him.
sentences.i: They began beating him with the hides, naked as he was, until he fainted.
sentences.n: غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ, literally "it was covered over him", is the regular expression for "he fainted", with an impersonal passive.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلُوهُ عَلَى حِمَارٍ حَتَّى وَدَّوْهُ إِلَى الْوَالِي
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamalūhu ʿalā ḥimārin ḥattā waddawhu ilā al-wālī
sentences.l: And they-carried-him upon a-donkey until they-took-him to the-governor.
sentences.i: Then they loaded him onto a donkey and took him to the governor.
sentences.n: وَدَّى (here "to take, bring") is a colloquial verb of the Egyptian type; the Classical word would be أَوْصَلَ or ذَهَبَ بِـ. Here حَتَّى means "until", but loosely, as a link between two stages.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْوَالِي مَا هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-wālī mā hādhā
sentences.l: And said to-them the governor: What (is) this?
sentences.i: The governor said to them, "What is this?"

sentences.t: قَالُوا وَقَعَ لَنَا مِنْ بَيْتِ الْوَزِيرِ وَهُوَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ
sentences.tr: qālū waqaʿa lanā min bayti al-wazīri wa-huwa ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati
sentences.l: They-said: He-fell to-us from the-house of-the-vizier, and he (was) upon this state.
sentences.i: They said, "He dropped in on us from the vizier's house, in this condition."
sentences.n: لَنَا ("to us") after وَقَعَ is the dative of the person affected: "he fell upon us, he landed on us". The vizier's house is where the old woman and the girl had taken him.

sentences.t: فَصَفَعَهُ مِائَةَ دِرَّةٍ ثُمَّ نَفَاهُ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣafaʿahu miʾata dirratin thumma nafāhu min baghdāda
sentences.l: And he-struck-him a-hundred (of) whip(-strokes), then he-banished-him from Baghdad.
sentences.i: The governor had him given a hundred lashes, and then banished him from Baghdad.
sentences.n: صَفَعَ is to slap or strike (originally on the nape); here the blows are with the whip, دِرَّة. The governor is the subject, though the print does not say so.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا خَلْفَهُ وَأَدْخَلْتُهُ الْمَدِينَةَ سِرًّا
sentences.tr: wa-kharajtu anā khalfahu wa-adkhaltuhu al-madīnata sirran
sentences.l: And I-went-out, I, behind-him, and I-made-him-enter the-city secretly.
sentences.i: I went out after him and brought him back into the city in secret,
sentences.n: The barber now takes the story in his own voice ("I"); the narration has passed from Shahrazād, to the barber, to his brother's tale.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَتَّبْتُ لَهُ مَا يَقْتَاتُ بِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma rattabtu lahu mā yaqtātu bihi
sentences.l: Then I-arranged for-him that-which he-lives with-it.
sentences.i: and then arranged an allowance for him to live on.
sentences.n: اِقْتَاتَ بِـ is "to live on, subsist on", with بِـ for the thing that sustains.

sentences.t: فَلَوْلَا مُرُوَّتِي مَاكُنْتُ أَحْتَمِلُ مِثْلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lawlā muruwwatī mā-kuntu aḥtamilu mithlahu
sentences.l: And if-not (for) my-manliness, I-would-not-have endured the-like of-him.
sentences.i: Were it not for my generosity of spirit, I would never have put up with someone like him.
sentences.n: The print joins ماكنت into one word. مُرُوَّتِي is printed without a hamza (the usual spelling is مُرُوءَة). Here كُنْتُ with an imperfect verb makes a past-habitual "would not have borne". مُرُوَّة is manly virtue, magnanimity.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَخِي الثَّالِثُ فَاسْمُهُ فَقِيقٌ وَكَانَ أَعْمَى
sentences.tr: wa-ammā akhī al-thālithu fa-ismuhu faqīqun wa-kāna aʿmā
sentences.l: And as-for my-brother the-third, so his-name (was) Faqīq, and he-was blind.
sentences.i: As for my third brother, his name was Faqīq, and he was blind.
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا ... فَـ is the Arabic "as for ... (then) ..." pattern, a way to turn the story to a new person. The name فقيق is printed without vowels; Faqīq is the natural reading.

sentences.t: فَسَاقَهُ الْقَضَاءُ وَالْقَدَرُ إِلَى دَارٍ كَبِيرَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-sāqahu al-qaḍāʾu wa-al-qadaru ilā dārin kabīratin
sentences.l: And drove-him the-decree and the-fate to a-house big.
sentences.i: Fate and destiny drove him to a big house.
sentences.n: الْقَضَاءُ وَالْقَدَرُ, "decree and destiny", is a stock pair for the divine ordinance that brings events about.

sentences.t: فَدَقَّ الْبَابَ طَمَعًا أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ صَاحِبُهَا فَيَسْأَ لَهُ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: fa-daqqa al-bāba ṭamaʿan an yukallimahu ṣāḥibuhā fa-yasʾa lahu shayʾan
sentences.l: And he-knocked the-door, in-hope that speak-to-him its-owner, so-he-ask him a-thing.
sentences.i: He knocked at the door, hoping that the owner would speak to him so that he could ask him for something.
sentences.n: The print splits فيسأله into two words, فيسا له; read it as one word, فَيَسْأَلَهُ, with the pronoun "him" cut off by a space. The subjunctive after فَـ answers the hope in أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ. طَمَعًا, "in hope, out of desire", is an adverbial accusative.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ صَاحِبُ الدَّارِ مَنْ بِالْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ṣāḥibu al-dāri man bi-al-bābi
sentences.l: And said the-owner of-the-house: Who (is) at-the-door?
sentences.i: The master of the house said, "Who is at the door?"

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يُكَلِّمْهُ أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yukallimhu aḥadun
sentences.l: And not spoke-to-him anyone.
sentences.i: Nobody answered him.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَهُ أَخِي يَقُولُ بِصَوْتٍ عَالِي مَنْ هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿahu akhī yaqūlu bi-ṣawtin ʿālī man hādhā
sentences.l: And heard-him my-brother saying with a-voice loud: Who (is) this?
sentences.i: My brother heard him calling out loudly, "Who is this?"
sentences.n: عَالِي is printed with the final yā in place of the Classical عَالٍ (indefinite defective adjective); the text writes this ending in full, as colloquial speech has it.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يُكَلِّمْهُ أَخِي وَسَمِعَ مَشْيَهُ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى الْبَابِ وَفَتَحَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yukallimhu akhī wa-samiʿa mashyahu ḥattā waṣala ilā al-bābi wa-fataḥahu
sentences.l: And not spoke-to-him my-brother; and he-heard his-walking until he-reached to the-door and opened-it.
sentences.i: My brother did not answer him, but he heard him walking until he reached the door and opened it.
sentences.n: The subject changes at وَسَمِعَ: the blind man hears the owner's footsteps, and it is the owner who comes to the door and opens it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu mā turīdu
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: What you-want?
sentences.i: He said to him, "What do you want?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي شَيْأً لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī shayʾan li-Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And said my-brother: A-thing for-God, exalted-is-He.
sentences.i: My brother said, "Something, for the sake of God Most High."
sentences.n: A beggar's formula: لِلَّهِ, "for God's sake". The print marks the hamza of شيأ on the alif, as before; the lām of لِلَّهِ is the لِـ of purpose, "for".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ ضَرِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu anta ḍarīrun
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: You (are) blind.
sentences.i: He said to him, "You are blind?"
sentences.n: ضَرِير, "blind, afflicted", is the polite word for a blind person.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ أَخِي نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu akhī naʿam
sentences.l: Said to-him my-brother: Yes.
sentences.i: My brother said, "Yes."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ نَاوِلْنِي يَدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu nāwilnī yadaka
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: Hand-me your-hand.
sentences.i: He said to him, "Give me your hand."

sentences.t: فَنَا وَلَهُ يَدَهُ وَهُوَ يَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّهُ يُعْطِيهِ شَيْــأً
sentences.tr: fa-nā wa-lahu yadahu wa-huwa yaʿtaqidu annahu yuʿṭīhi shayʾan
sentences.l: And he-han- -ded-him his-hand, and he believing that-he (would) give-him a-thing.
sentences.i: So he held out his hand, believing that the man was going to give him something.
sentences.n: The print breaks فناوله into two words, فنا وله; read it as the single word فَنَاوَلَهُ, "and he handed him". Likewise شيــأ is printed with an elongating stroke (ـ) inside the word; the stroke is kept and the word is the same شَيْأً.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ فَأَدْخَلَهُ الدَّارَ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَصْعَدُ بِهِ مِنْ سُلَّمٍ إِلَى سُلَّمٍ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى أَعْلَا سُطُوحٍ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha bi-yadihi fa-adkhalahu al-dāra wa-lam yazal yaṣʿadu bihi min sullamin ilā sullamin ḥattā waṣala ilā aʿlā suṭūḥin
sentences.l: And he-took by-his-hand and made-him-enter the-house, and not he-ceased (to) ascend with-him from a-stair to a-stair until he-reached to the-top (of) roofs.
sentences.i: Then he took him by the hand, led him into the house, and kept taking him up from one flight of stairs to the next until they reached the top of the roofs.
sentences.n: أَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ is "to take someone by the hand", with بِـ for the part held. صَعِدَ بِهِ means "he took him up" (بِـ makes the verb transitive). The print writes أعلا with a plain alif (Classical أعلى); سُطُوح is the plural of سَطْح, "roof", so "the topmost of the roofs", i.e. the highest level of the house.

sentences.t: وَأَخِي يَقُولُ إِنَّهُ يُطْعِمُهُ شَيْأً أَوْ يُعْطِيهِ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: wa-akhī yaqūlu innahu yuṭʿimuhu shayʾan aw yuʿṭīhi shayʾan
sentences.l: And my-brother saying (to himself) that-he (would) feed-him a-thing or give-him a-thing.
sentences.i: All the while my brother told himself that the man would feed him something or give him something.
sentences.n: يَقُولُ here is "says (to himself)", that is, "thinks"; the sentence is a circumstantial clause with its own subject.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْتَهَى قَالَ لِأَخِي مَا تُرِيدُ يَا ضَرِيرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā intahā qāla li-akhī mā turīdu yā ḍarīru
sentences.l: And when he-arrived he-said to-my-brother: What you-want, O blind-one?
sentences.i: When they had arrived at the top, he said to my brother, "What do you want, blind man?"

sentences.t: قَالَ أُرِيدُ شَيْأً لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: qāla urīdu shayʾan li-Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: He-said: I-want a-thing for-God, exalted-is-He.
sentences.i: He said, "I want something, for God's sake."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَفْتَحُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yaftaḥu Allāhu ʿalayka
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: Opens God upon-you.
sentences.i: He said to him, "May God open a way for you."
sentences.n: This is the stock polite refusal to a beggar, roughly "God will provide (but I will not)"; the beggar, who expected a gift, has been led up all those stairs for nothing.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي يَا هَذَا مَا كُنْتَ تَقُــولُ لِي كَذَا وَكَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī yā hādhā mā kunta taqūlu lī kadhā wa-kadhā
sentences.l: And said to-him my-brother: O this-one, what you-were saying to-me thus and thus?
sentences.i: My brother said to him, "Man, weren't you saying to me, thus and so ..."
sentences.n: يَا هَذَا, "O you there", is a curt form of address. The print puts a stroke inside تقــول, kept here. كَذَا وَكَذَا, "such and such", stands for words the speaker does not spell out; the sentence carries on in the next lines of the night.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَسْفَلُ
sentences.tr: wa-anā asfalu
sentences.l: And I, (am) below.
sentences.i: while I was down below.
sentences.n: The slice opens in the middle of a sentence. أَسْفَلُ is the elative "lower", used as an adverb: "below".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا سَفِلَةُ لِمَ لَا تُكَلِّمُنِي مِنْ أَوَّلِ مَرَّةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā safilatu li-ma lā tukallimunī min awwali marratin
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: O base-ones, to-what (= why) not you-speak-to-me from first time?
sentences.i: He said to him, "You scum! Why didn't you speak to me the first time?"
sentences.n: سَفِلَة is "the base ones, the riffraff", a collective noun used as an insult to a single person. لِمَ is لِـ + مَا, "why", the alif of مَا dropped after the preposition. مِنْ أَوَّلِ مَرَّةٍ, "from the first time", means "right away, in the first place".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي وَالسَّاعَةَ مَا تُرِيدُ تَصْنَعُ بِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī wa-al-sāʿata mā turīdu taṣnaʿu bī
sentences.l: And said to-him my-brother: And the-hour, what you-want you-do with-me?
sentences.i: My brother said to him, "And now, what do you want to do to me?"
sentences.n: تُرِيدُ تَصْنَعُ sets two imperfects side by side with no أَنْ ("you want, you do"), the usual Middle Arabic way to say "you want to do". وَالسَّاعَةَ, "and the hour", is "and right now".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا عِنْدِي شَيٌ أُعْطِيهِ لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu mā ʿindī shayʾun uʿṭīhi laka
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: There-is-not with-me a-thing I-give-it to-you.
sentences.i: He said, "I have nothing to give you."
sentences.n: The print writes شيء without its hamza but puts a nunation mark on the yāʾ; we keep that mark where it stands. Read shayʾun, "a thing". أُعْطِيهِ لَكَ, "I give it to you", is a relative clause with no linking word, as is normal after an indefinite noun.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ انْزِلْ بِي إِلَى السَّلَا لِمِ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu inzil bī ilā al-salā limi
sentences.l: He-said to-him: Go-down with-me to the-stairs.
sentences.i: He said to him, "Take me down to the stairs."
sentences.n: The print splits السلالم, "the stairs" (plural of سُلَّم), into two words, السلا لم. We keep the split and point the second half with the genitive ending (لِمِ), so that the two halves read together as al-salālimi. انْزِلْ بِي, "go down with me", means "take me down": بِـ carries the person along with the action.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الطَّرِيقُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṭarīqu bayna yadayka
sentences.l: And he-said: The-road (is) between your-two-hands.
sentences.i: He said, "The way is right in front of you."
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ, "between your two hands", is the common idiom for "right in front of you".

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَخِي وَأَقْبَلَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma akhī wa-aqbala
sentences.l: And rose my-brother and advanced.
sentences.i: So my brother got up and set off,

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ نَازِلًا حَتَّى بَقِيَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْبَابِ عِشْرُونَ دَرَجَةً
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla nāzilan ḥattā baqiya baynahu wa-bayna al-bābi ʿishrūna darajatan
sentences.l: And he-did-not cease descending, until there-remained between-him and between the-door twenty steps.
sentences.i: and he kept going down until twenty steps were left between him and the door.
sentences.n: مَا زَالَ + accusative participle is "he kept on doing". The number عِشْرُونَ is the subject of بَقِيَ and so stands in the nominative; the counted noun دَرَجَةً follows in the accusative singular.

sentences.t: فَزَلِقَتْ رِجْلُهُ فَوَقَعَ إِلَى الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-zaliqat rijluhu fa-waqaʿa ilā al-bābi
sentences.l: And slipped his-foot, and he-fell to the-door.
sentences.i: His foot slipped and he tumbled down as far as the door.

sentences.t: فَانْفَتَحَ رَأْسُهُ فَخَرَجَ وَهُوَ لَا يَدْرِي أَيْنَ يَذْهَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-infataḥa raʾsuhu fa-kharaja wa-huwa lā yadrī ayna yadhhabu
sentences.l: And opened his-head, and he-went-out, and he not knowing where he-goes.
sentences.i: His head split open, and he staggered out, not knowing where he was going.
sentences.n: انْفَتَحَ رَأْسُهُ, "his head was opened", is "his head was split". The hamza of رَأْسُهُ is printed precomposed in the edition and is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَحِقَهُ بَعْضُ رُفْقَتِهِ الْعُمْيَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-laḥiqahu baʿḍu rufqatihi al-ʿumyānu
sentences.l: And caught-up-with-him some-of his-company, the blind-ones.
sentences.i: Some of his blind companions caught up with him
sentences.n: الْعُمْيَان is the plural of أَعْمَى, "blind", used here as a noun in apposition: "his companions, the blind men".

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهُ أَيْشَ حَصَلَ لَكَ الْيَوْمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahu aysh ḥaṣala laka al-yawma
sentences.l: And they-said to-him: What happened to-you today?
sentences.i: and asked him, "What has happened to you today?"
sentences.n: أَيْشَ is the colloquial contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ, "which thing?" = "what?"; Classical would say مَاذَا. حَصَلَ لَكَ, "it came about for you", is the spoken-language "happened to you".

sentences.t: فَحَدَّثَهُمْ بِمَا وَقَعَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaddathahum bi-mā waqaʿa lahu
sentences.l: And he-told-them of-what fell to-him.
sentences.i: He told them what had befallen him,

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُمْ يَا إِخْوَتِي أُرِيدُأَنْ أُخْرِجَ شَيْأً مِنَ الدَّرَاهِمِ الَّتِي بَقِيَتْ مَعِي وَأُنْفِقَ عَلَى نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahum yā ikhwatī urīdu an ukhrija shayʾan mina al-darāhimi al-latī baqiyat maʿī wa-unfiqa ʿalā nafsī
sentences.l: Then he-said to-them: O my-brothers, I-want that I-take-out something from the-dirhams which remained with-me, and I-spend on my-self.
sentences.i: then said to them, "My brothers, I want to take out some of the dirhams I have left, and spend them on myself."
sentences.n: The print runs اريد and ان together as one word, اريدان. We point it so that it reads as the two words أُرِيدُ أَنْ, "I want to"; the same happens again below (يريدان). شَيْأً is the print's spelling of شَيْئًا, "something", with the hamza on an alif-shaped seat. We keep that character as printed.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ صَاحِبُ الدَّارِتَا بِعَهُ وَسَامِعَ كَلَامِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ṣāḥibu al-dāri tā biʿahu wa-sāmiʿa kalāmihi
sentences.l: And was the-master-of the-house following-him and hearing-of his-speech.
sentences.i: Meanwhile the master of the house was following him and listening to what he said,
sentences.n: The print breaks تابعه, "following him", after its first syllable and glues that syllable onto الدار, giving الدارتا بعه. Read al-dāri tābiʿahu. Both participles, تَابِعَهُ and سَامِعَ, are accusative (they complete كَانَ) and keep their ending because the pronoun or noun after them is attached to them in a possessive-style phrase: "following-him", "hearer-of his speech".

sentences.t: وَأَخِي لَايَدْرِي بِالرَّجُلِ وَرَفِيقِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhī lā yadrī bi-al-rajuli wa-rafīqihi
sentences.l: And my-brother not knowing of-the-man and his-companion.
sentences.i: while my brother knew nothing of the man or of his companion.
sentences.n: لَايَدْرِي is printed as one word. دَرَى بِـ is "to be aware of": the verb chooses the preposition.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ أَخِي إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَدَخَلَ وَدَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ خَلْفَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa akhī ilā manzilihi wa-dakhala wa-dakhala al-rajulu khalfahu
sentences.l: And came my-brother to his-dwelling, and entered, and entered the-man behind-him.
sentences.i: My brother came to his house and went in, and the man went in behind him,
sentences.n: The print has وَدَخَلَ twice, the first at the end of one page and the second at the start of the next, a repeated word probably caused by the page turn. We keep both as printed; read once, the sense is the same.

sentences.t: وَأَخِي لَايَشْعُرُ بِهِ وَقَعَدَ أَخِي يَنْتَظِرُ رُفَقَاءَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-akhī lā yashʿuru bihi wa-qaʿada akhī yantaẓiru rufaqāʾahu
sentences.l: And my-brother not perceiving of-him; and sat my-brother awaiting his-companions.
sentences.i: without my brother noticing him. My brother sat down to wait for his companions.
sentences.n: شَعَرَ بِـ is "to be aware of", like دَرَى بِـ above. قَعَدَ + imperfect, "he sat waiting", has the Middle Arabic sense "he settled down to".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا قَالَ لَهُمُ اغْلِقُوا الْبَابَ وَفَتِّشُوا الْبَيْتَ كَيْلَا يَكُونَ تَبِعَنَا أَحَدٌ غَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalū qāla lahumu ighliqū al-bāba wa-fattishū al-bayta kayla yakūna tabiʿanā aḥadun gharībun
sentences.l: And when they-entered he-said to-them: Lock the-door and search the-house, so-that-not there-be followed-us anyone strange.
sentences.i: When they had come in he said to them, "Lock the door and search the house, in case a stranger has followed us."
sentences.n: كَيْلَا يَكُونَ takes the subjunctive; the perfect تَبِعَنَا then states what must not be the case: "lest there be someone, a stranger, who has followed us".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّــا سَمِعَ الرَّجُلُ كَلَامَ أَخِي قَامَ وَتَعَلَّقَ بِحَبْلٍ كَانَ فِى السَّقْفِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-rajulu kalāma akhī qāma wa-taʿallaqa bi-ḥablin kāna fī al-saqfi
sentences.l: And when heard the-man the-speech-of my-brother, he-rose and clung to-a-rope that-was in the-ceiling.
sentences.i: When the man heard what my brother said, he got up and caught hold of a rope that hung from the ceiling.
sentences.n: The print stretches فلمّا with a tatweel (فلمــا) and spells فِى with a dotless final yāʾ; we keep both as printed. تَعَلَّقَ بِـ is "to cling to, hang on to".

sentences.t: فَطَافُوا الْبَيْتَ جَمِيعَهُ فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا وَاحِدًا
sentences.tr: fa-ṭāfū al-bayta jamīʿahu fa-lam yajidū wāḥidan
sentences.l: And they-went-round the-house, all-of-it, and did-not find one.
sentences.i: They went all around the house and found no one.
sentences.n: وَاحِدًا, "one", is "anyone" after the negative.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَجَعُوا وَجَلَسُوا إِلَى جَانِبِ أَخِي
sentences.tr: thumma rajaʿū wa-jalasū ilā jānibi akhī
sentences.l: Then they-returned and sat to the-side-of my-brother.
sentences.i: Then they went back and sat down beside my brother,

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخْرَجُوا الدَّرَاهِمَ الَّتِى مَعَهُمْ وَعَدُّوهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ اثْنَىْ عَشَرَ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: thumma akhrajū al-darāhima al-latī maʿahum wa-ʿaddūhā fa-idhā hiya ithnay ʿashara alfa dirhamin
sentences.l: Then they-took-out the-dirhams that (were) with-them and counted-them, and-behold they (were) twelve thousand dirhams.
sentences.i: then took out the dirhams they had with them and counted them, and found they came to twelve thousand dirhams.
sentences.n: The print has the oblique form اثنى (ithnay) after فَإِذَا هِيَ, where Classical would use the nominative اثنا; Middle Arabic uses the oblique form in every position, and we point what is printed. هِيَ, feminine singular, refers back to the plural الدراهم: a plural of things takes feminine singular agreement. In twelve thousand, ألف is the counted noun, accusative singular after the number, and دِرْهَمٍ is in the genitive after it.

sentences.t: فَتَرَكُوهَا فِي زَاوِيَةِ الْبَيْتِ وَأَخَذَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-tarakūhā fī zāwiyati al-bayti wa-akhadha kullu wāḥidin mā yaḥtāju ilayhi
sentences.l: And they-left-it in the-corner-of the-house, and took each one what he-needs to-it.
sentences.i: They left the money in a corner of the house, and each man took what he needed
sentences.n: اِحْتَاجَ إِلَى is "to need": the verb chooses the preposition, so إِلَيْهِ is not "to him" but "[he needs] of it".

sentences.t: وَطَرَحُوا بَقِيَّةَ الدَّرَاهِمِ فِى التُّرَابِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭaraḥū baqiyyata al-darāhimi fī al-turābi
sentences.l: And they-threw the-remainder-of the-dirhams in the-dust.
sentences.i: and threw the rest of the dirhams into the dirt.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَدَّمُوا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ شَيْأً مِنَ الْأَكْلِ وَقَعَدُوا يَأْكُلُونَ
sentences.tr: thumma qaddamū bayna aydīhim shayʾan mina al-akli wa-qaʿadū yaʾkulūna
sentences.l: Then they-set-forward between their-hands something of the-eating, and sat they-eat.
sentences.i: Then they set out some food in front of them and sat down to eat.
sentences.n: شَيْأً is the print's spelling of شَيْئًا, with the hamza printed on an alif-shaped seat. We keep that character exactly as printed. مِنَ الْأَكْلِ, "something of the eating", is "some food".

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ أَخِي اِىٰ جَانِبِهِ مَضْغًا غَرِيبًا
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa akhī ilā jānibihi maḍghan gharīban
sentences.l: And heard my-brother, to his-side, a-chewing strange.
sentences.i: Then my brother heard a strange chewing sound close beside him
sentences.n: The print has اى where الى (إِلَى, "to") is expected, so a lām has dropped out. We cannot add a letter, so the ى carries a dagger alif and the word sounds ilā; read "to his side" = "close beside him". مَضْغ is "chewing".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ مَعَنَا غَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-aṣḥābihi maʿanā gharībun
sentences.l: And he-said to-his-companions: With-us (is) a-stranger.
sentences.i: and said to his companions, "There is a stranger with us."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَدَّ يَدَهُ فَتَعَلَّقَ بِيَدِهِ يَدِ الرَّجُلِ صَاحِبِ الدَّارِ
sentences.tr: thumma madda yadahu fa-taʿallaqa bi-yadihi yadi al-rajuli ṣāḥibi al-dāri
sentences.l: Then he-stretched his-hand, and clung to-his-hand, the-hand-of the-man, the-master-of the-house.
sentences.i: Then he stretched out his hand and seized the hand of the man, the master of the house.
sentences.n: The grammar of فَتَعَلَّقَ بِيَدِهِ يَدِ الرَّجُلِ is rough. We read "he seized his hand, (that is) the hand of the man", the second noun in apposition to the first and the pronoun looking ahead to الرجل. The sense is certainly that the brother's groping hand closes on the stranger's. The print may have lost a word or two (for example فتعلقت يده بيد الرجل, "his hand caught the man's hand").

sentences.t: فَوَقَعُوا فِيهِ ضَرْبًا
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿū fīhi ḍarban
sentences.l: And they-fell upon-him (in) beating.
sentences.i: and they fell on him with blows.
sentences.n: وَقَعَ فِي is "to fall upon, attack". ضَرْبًا, "in beating", is an accusative of manner.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَالَ عَلَيْهِمْ ذَلِكَ صَاحُوا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭāla ʿalayhim dhālika ṣāḥū
sentences.l: And when that grew-long upon-them, they-shouted:
sentences.i: When this went on too long for them, they shouted,

sentences.t: يَا مُسْلِمِينَ دَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا لِصٌّ يُرِيدُأَنْ يَأْخُذَ مَالَنَا
sentences.tr: yā muslimīna dakhala ʿalaynā liṣṣun yurīdu an yaʾkhudha mālanā
sentences.l: O Muslims! Entered upon-us a-thief; he-wants that he-take our-wealth.
sentences.i: "O Muslims! A thief has broken in on us, and means to take our money!"
sentences.n: يُرِيدُأَنْ is again printed as one word: read يُرِيدُ أَنْ, "he wants to". دَخَلَ عَلَى is "to enter upon" someone, i.e. to burst in on them in their own house.

sentences.t: فَاجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِمْ خَلْقٌ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ijtamaʿa ʿalayhim khalqun kathīrun
sentences.l: And gathered upon-them a-creation, many.
sentences.i: A great crowd gathered around them.
sentences.n: خَلْق is literally "creation, created things"; in this register it is simply "people, a crowd".

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ الرَّجُلُ وَتَعَلَّقَ بِهِمْ وَادَّعَى عَلَيْهِمْ مِثْلَمَا ادَّعَوْا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala al-rajulu wa-taʿallaqa bihim wa-iddaʿā ʿalayhim mithlamā iddaʿaw ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And advanced the-man and clung to-them and claimed against-them like-what they-claimed against-him.
sentences.i: The man came forward, seized hold of them, and brought the same charge against them that they had brought against him,
sentences.n: اِدَّعَى عَلَى is "to make a claim or charge against".

sentences.t: وَغَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ حَتَّى كَأَنَّهُ صَارَ مِثْلَهُمْ لَا يَشُكُّ فِيهَا أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ghammaḍa ʿaynayhi ḥattā ka-annahu ṣāra mithlahum lā yashukku fīhā aḥadun
sentences.l: And he-shut his-two-eyes, until as-if-he became like-them, not doubts in-it anyone.
sentences.i: and shut his eyes so that he seemed to have become just like them, and no one doubted it.
sentences.n: كَ + أَنَّ, "as if", introduces how he looked. مِثْلَهُمْ, "like them", means blind like them. The feminine فِيهَا, "in it", points back to the feminine idea of the whole pretence and is best left as "it".

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ يَا مُسْلِمِينَ أَنَا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالسُّلْطَانِ أَنَا بِاللَّهِ وَالْوَالِي مَعَ نَصِيحَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa yā muslimīna anā bi-Allāhi wa-bi-al-sulṭāni anā bi-Allāhi wa-al-wālī maʿa naṣīḥatin
sentences.l: And he-cried: O Muslims, I (am) by-God and by-the-sultan; I (am) by-God and the-governor, with sincerity.
sentences.i: He cried out, "O Muslims, I call on God and the Sultan! I call on God and the governor, in good faith!"
sentences.n: أَنَا بِاللَّهِ is elliptic, a cry for help: "I (appeal) by God". The last phrase, مَعَ نَصِيحَةٍ, is obscure: نَصِيحَة is "sincerity, honest counsel", so "in all sincerity" or "with a warning"; we have taken the first.

sentences.t: فَمَا شَعَرَ إِلَّا وَقَدْ أَحَاطُوا بِالْجَمِيعِ وَأَخِي مَعَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-mā shaʿara illā wa-qad aḥāṭū bi-al-jamīʿi wa-akhī maʿahum
sentences.l: And he-did-not perceive except-that they-had surrounded all, with my-brother with-them.
sentences.i: Before anyone knew it, they were surrounded, all of them, my brother with them,
sentences.n: مَا شَعَرَ إِلَّا وَقَدْ is "he knew nothing before...", i.e. "suddenly". أَحَاطَ بِـ is "to surround": the verb chooses the preposition.

sentences.t: وَسَاقُوا إِلَى بَيْتِ الْوَالِي فَأَحْضَرَهُمْ قُدَّامَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-sāqū ilā bayti al-wālī fa-aḥḍarahum quddāmahu
sentences.l: And they-drove to the-house-of the-governor, and he-had-them-brought in-front-of-him.
sentences.i: and they were driven to the governor's house, where he had them brought before him.
sentences.n: سَاقُوا has no object in the print; supply "them". قُدَّامَهُ, "in front of him", is the everyday word for "before, in the presence of".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مَا خَبَرُكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla mā khabarukum
sentences.l: And he-said: What (is) your-news?
sentences.i: He said, "What is your story?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ انْظُرْ وَلَا يُبَانُ لَكَ شَىً إِلَّا بِالْعُقُوبَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-rajulu unẓur wa-lā yubānu laka shayʾan illā bi-al-ʿuqūbati
sentences.l: And said the-man: Look, and not is-made-clear to-you a-thing except by-the-punishment.
sentences.i: The man said, "Look: you will learn nothing except by punishment.
sentences.n: The print marks شىً with a fathatan; we keep that mark where it stands. A passive subject would normally be nominative (shayʾun), so the form is a little off; يُبَانُ, "is made clear", may also be a slip for يَبِينُ, "becomes clear". The sense is the same either way. بِالْعُقُوبَةِ: بِـ means "by means of".

sentences.t: وَأَوَّلُ مَا تَبْدَأُ اِبْدَأْبِي وَعَاتِبْنِى ثُمَّ لِهَذَا قَائِدِي
sentences.tr: wa-awwalu mā tabdaʾu ibdaʾ bī wa-ʿātibnī thumma li-hādhā qāʾidī
sentences.l: And first (of) what you-begin, begin with-me, and reproach me; then for-this-one, my-guide.
sentences.i: The very first thing you do, begin with me: chastise me first, and then this man, my guide."
sentences.n: اِبْدَأْبِي is printed as one word (ابدأ بي). وَعَاتِبْنِى is "and reproach me"; in a speech about being beaten one would expect عَاقِبْنِي, "punish me", and the print may have confused the two. The speaker is bidding the governor beat him first. ثُمَّ لِهَذَا قَائِدِي is elliptic: "then (do the same) to this man, my guide". The edition prints the hamza of تَبْدَأُ, ابْدَأْ and قَائِدِي precomposed, and we keep it as printed.

sentences.t: وَأَوْمَى بِيَدِهِ إِلَى
sentences.tr: wa-awmā bi-yadihi ilā
sentences.l: And he-motioned with-his-hand to
sentences.i: And he motioned with his hand toward
sentences.n: أَوْمَى is the weak-verb spelling of Classical أَوْمَأَ, "to signal". The slice ends here, in mid-sentence.

sentences.t: أَخِي
sentences.tr: akhī
sentences.l: my-brother
sentences.i: my brother
sentences.n: The slice opens in the middle of a sentence: this word completes a clause begun just before it, so read it with what precedes. أَخِي is "my brother"; the print gives no case, so I point the form that fits any role.

sentences.t: فَمَدُّوا ذٰلِكَ الرَّجُلَ وَضَرَبُوهُ أَرْبَعَمِائَةِ عَصًا عَلَى ثَقْبِهِ فَأَوْجَعَهُ الضَّرْبُ
sentences.tr: fa-maddū dhālika al-rajula wa-ḍarabūhu arbaʿa miʾati ʿaṣan ʿalā thaqbihi fa-awjaʿahu al-ḍarbu
sentences.l: And they-stretched-out that man and they-struck-him four-hundred of-stick on his-hole, and the-beating pained-him.
sentences.i: They stretched that man out and gave him four hundred strokes of the stick on his arse, and the beating hurt him badly.
sentences.n: ثَقْبِهِ is literally "his hole", here the man's behind, where the blows fall; the print is blunt and so is the literal layer. "Four hundred of stick" counts blows by the stick (عَصًا). مَدُّوا is "they stretched him out", laid him flat for the flogging.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ عَيْنَهُ الْوَاحِدَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa ʿaynahu al-wāḥidata
sentences.l: And he-opened his-eye, the-one.
sentences.i: Then he opened one eye.
sentences.n: الْوَاحِدَةَ, "the one", means one of his two eyes. The man has been pretending to be blind.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا زَادُوا عَلَيْهِ بِالضَّرْبِ فَتَحَ عَيْنَهُ الْأُخْرَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā zādū ʿalayhi bi-al-ḍarbi fataḥa ʿaynahu al-ukhrā
sentences.l: And when they-increased upon-him with-the-beating, he-opened his-eye, the-other.
sentences.i: And when they piled on more blows, he opened the other eye too.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَالِي مَا هٰذِهِ الْفِعَالُ يَا مَلْعُونُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wālī mā hādhihi al-fiʿālu yā malʿūnu
sentences.l: And said to-him the-governor: What (are) these deeds, O cursed-one?
sentences.i: The governor said to him, "What is all this, you cursed man?"
sentences.n: الْوَالِي is the city governor, who also keeps order and judges. هٰذِهِ (feminine singular) with الْفِعَالُ, "the deeds", is normal: a plural of things takes the feminine singular.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَعْطِنِى خَاتَمَ الْأَمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla aʿṭinī khātama al-amāni
sentences.l: And he-said: Give-me the-ring (of) the-safety.
sentences.i: He said, "Give me the seal of safe-conduct,"
sentences.n: خَاتَم is a signet ring or seal; the "ring of safety" seems to be the token of an amnesty (أَمَان), so he is asking for immunity before he confesses. The print ends أعطنى in ى; I keep that spelling.

sentences.t: نَحْنُ أَرْبَعَةٌ نَعْمَلُ أَرْوَاحَنَا عُمْيَانٌ
sentences.tr: naḥnu arbaʿatun naʿmalu arwāḥanā ʿumyānun
sentences.l: We (are) four; we-make our-spirits blind-ones.
sentences.i: "There are four of us, and we pass ourselves off as blind men;
sentences.n: أَرْوَاحَنَا, "our spirits", is simply "ourselves". Classical grammar would put عُمْيَان in the accusative (عُمْيَانًا); the print has no alif, so I point the bare nominative, as Middle Arabic often does.

sentences.t: وَنُغِيرُ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَنَدْخُلُ الْبُيُوتَ وَنَنْظُرُ النِّسَاءَ وَنَعْمَلُ فِي خَسَارَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-nughīru ʿalā al-nāsi wa-nadkhulu al-buyūta wa-nanẓuru al-nisāʾa wa-naʿmalu fī khasāratihim
sentences.l: and we-raid upon the-people, and we-enter the-houses, and we-look-at the-women, and we-work in their-ruin.
sentences.i: we raid people, walk into their houses, look our fill at their women, and work for their ruin.
sentences.n: نُغِيرُ عَلَى (from أَغَارَ عَلَى) is "to swoop on, raid". The last clause is loose: نَعْمَلُ فِي خَسَارَتِهِمْ, "we work in their loss", i.e. we profit from their misfortune; خَسَارَة can also mean "disgrace".

sentences.t: فَاجْتَمَعَ لَنَا مَكْسَبٌ عَظِيمٌ وَهُوَ اثْنَىْ عَشَرَ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ijtamaʿa lanā maksabun ʿaẓīmun wa-huwa ithnay ʿashara alfa dirhamin
sentences.l: So there-gathered to-us a-profit great, and it (is) twelve thousand dirham.
sentences.i: So a great profit came to us, twelve thousand dirhams in all."
sentences.n: The print writes اثنى with final ى; it is the "twelve" of اثنا عشر in the oblique form, here used as a fixed number. Twelve thousand split four ways is the three thousand he claims in the next line.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لِرِفْقَتِى أَعْطُونِي حَقِّي ثَلٰثَةَ آلَافٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu li-rifqatī aʿṭūnī ḥaqqī thalāthata ālāfin
sentences.l: And I-said to-my-company: Give-me my-right, three thousands.
sentences.i: "I said to my companions, 'Give me my due: three thousand.'
sentences.n: لِرِفْقَتِى: لِـ marks the person addressed, "to my company". The print writes ثلثة without the alif of ثلاثة, so a dagger alif (ٰ) is pointed over the second letter.

sentences.t: فَقَامُوا وَضَرَبُونِي وَأَخَذُوا مَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāmū wa-ḍarabūnī wa-akhadhū mālī
sentences.l: And they-rose and they-struck-me and they-took my-wealth.
sentences.i: They rose up, beat me, and took my money,

sentences.t: وَأَنَا مُسْتَجِيرٌ بِاللَّهِ وَبِكَ وَأَنَا أَحَقُّ بِقِسْمِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā mustajīrun bi-Allāhi wa-bika wa-anā aḥaqqu bi-qismī
sentences.l: and I (am) one-seeking-refuge with-God and with-you, and I (am) more-entitled to-my-portion.
sentences.i: and now I take refuge with God and with you, for I have the better right to my share.
sentences.n: اِسْتَجَارَ بِـ takes the person one flees to for protection, hence "seek refuge with". أَحَقُّ بِـ is "more entitled to".

sentences.t: وَأَنَاأَشْتَهِي أَنْ تَعْرِفَ صِدْقَ قَوْلِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā ashtahī an taʿrifa ṣidqa qawlī
sentences.l: And I-I-desire that you-know the-truth (of) my-saying.
sentences.i: I want you to learn that I am telling the truth.
sentences.n: The print runs وأنا and أشتهي together as one word, وانااشتهي. The reading is وَأَنَا أَشْتَهِي, "and I desire", which I point as printed, joined.

sentences.t: فَاضْرِبْ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا ضَرَبْتَنِي فَإِنَّهُ يَفْتَحُ عَيْنَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-uḍrib kulla wāḥidin akthara mimmā ḍarabtanī fa-innahu yaftaḥu ʿaynayhi
sentences.l: So strike every one more than-what you-struck-me, for-he opens his-two-eyes.
sentences.i: Beat each of them harder than you beat me, for then he will open his eyes."
sentences.n: ضَرَبْتَنِي is "you struck me": the governor is told to beat the others harder than he beat this man, who has just had four hundred blows.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ أَمَرَالْوَالِي بِعُقُوبَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika amara al-wālī bi-ʿuqūbatihim
sentences.l: And at that, ordered-the-governor with-their-punishment.
sentences.i: At that the governor ordered them punished.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ الْوَالِي is printed as one word (امرالوالي). أَمَرَ بِـ is "to order (something)", here the punishment.

sentences.t: وَأَوَّلَ مَابَدَأَ بِأَخِي فَشَدُّوهُ عَلَى سُلَّمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-awwala mā badaʾa bi-akhī fa-shaddūhu ʿalā sullamin
sentences.l: And first (of) what he-began with my-brother; and-they-bound-him on a-ladder.
sentences.i: The first he began with was my brother, and they tied him to a ladder.
sentences.n: مَابَدَأَ is printed as one word, and the print has the precomposed أ there, which I keep. أَوَّلَ مَا بَدَأَ is "the first thing he began with". بَدَأَ بِـ is "begin with". The ladder serves as a frame for flogging.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْوَالِي يَا فَسَقَةُ تَجْحَدُونَ نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ وَتَدَّعُونَ أَنَّكُمْ عُمْيَانٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahumu al-wālī yā fasaqatu tajḥadūna niʿmata Allāhi wa-tadaʿʿūna annakum ʿumyānun
sentences.l: And said to-them the-governor: O sinners, you-deny the-favour of-God, and you-claim that-you (are) blind-ones.
sentences.i: And the governor said to them, "You reprobates! You deny God's gift and claim to be blind?"
sentences.n: فَسَقَة is the plural of فَاسِق, one who breaks the law or lives dissolutely. "God's favour" is their eyesight. تَدَّعُونَ is "you claim" (from اِدَّعَى).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي اللَّهَ اللَّهَ وَاللَّهِ مَا فِينَا بَصِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī Allāha Allāha wa-Allāhi mā fīnā baṣīrun
sentences.l: And said my-brother: God, God! and-by-God, not in-us (is) a-seeing-one.
sentences.i: My brother said, "For God's sake, for God's sake! By God, there is not one of us who can see!"
sentences.n: اللَّهَ اللَّهَ is an exclamation, "God! God!", an appeal to fear God; the accusative comes from an unspoken verb such as اِتَّقِ, "fear". بَصِير is "sighted", the opposite of blind.

sentences.t: فَضَرَبُوهُ حَتَّى غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍarabūhu ḥattā ghushiya ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And they-struck-him until it-was-covered over-him.
sentences.i: They beat him until he fainted.
sentences.n: غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ is a passive, literally "it was covered over him", the idiom for fainting.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَالِي دَعُوهُ حَتَّى يُفِيقَ وَأَعِيدُوا عَلَيْهِ الضَّرْبَ ثَانِيَ مَرَّةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wālī daʿūhu ḥattā yufīqa wa-aʿīdū ʿalayhi al-ḍarba thāniya marratin
sentences.l: And said the-governor: Leave-him until he-recovers, and repeat upon-him the-beating, a-second time.
sentences.i: The governor said, "Leave him until he comes round, then beat him a second time."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِضَرْبِ أَصْحَابِهِ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ثَلٰثِمِائَةِ عَصًا
sentences.tr: thumma amara bi-ḍarbi aṣḥābihi kulli wāḥidin akthara min thalāthi miʾati ʿaṣan
sentences.l: Then he-ordered the-beating (of) his-companions, each one more than three-hundred of-stick.
sentences.i: Then he ordered his companions beaten, each of them with more than three hundred strokes of the stick,

sentences.t: وَالْبَصِيرُ يَقُولُ لَهُمُ افْتَحُوا عُيُونَكُمْ وَإِلَّاجَدَّدَ عَلَيْكُمُ الضَّرْبَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-baṣīru yaqūlu lahumu iftaḥū ʿuyūnakum wa-illā jaddada ʿalaykumu al-ḍarba
sentences.l: while the-seeing-one says to-them: Open your-eyes, or-else he-renew upon-you the-beating.
sentences.i: while the man who could see kept telling them, "Open your eyes, or he will start the beating on you all over again!"
sentences.n: The print joins وإلا and جدد into one word, والاجدد. I read it as وَإِلَّا جَدَّدَ, "or else he will renew", with the governor as the one who renews the beating. الْبَصِيرُ, "the seeing one", is the man who, at the start, called himself blind.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ الرَّجُلُ لِلْوَالِي ابْعَثْ مَعِي مَنْ يَأْ تِيكَ بِالْمَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla al-rajulu li-al-wālī ibʿath maʿī man yaʾ tīka bi-al-māli
sentences.l: Then said the-man to-the-governor: Send with-me one-who brings-you with-the-money.
sentences.i: Then the man said to the governor, "Send someone with me to bring you the money,
sentences.n: The print splits يأتيك into two words, يا تيك (the hamza is ours). أَتَى بِـ is "bring": the verb chooses the preposition, so بِالْمَالِ is "with the money", i.e. "brings the money".

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ هٰؤُلَاءِ مَا يَفْتَحُونَ عُيُونَهُمْ وَيَخَافُونَ مِنْ فَضِيحَةِ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna hāʾulāʾi mā yaftaḥūna ʿuyūnahum wa-yakhāfūna min faḍīḥati al-nāsi
sentences.l: for these-ones not they-open their-eyes, and they-fear from the-disgrace (of) the-people.
sentences.i: for these men will never open their eyes, because they fear being shamed in front of everyone."
sentences.n: مَا يَفْتَحُونَ is "they do not (and will not) open"; the negative مَا with the imperfect is the usual way of saying it in Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَبَعَثَ الْوَالِي أَخَذَ الْمَالَ وَأَعْطَى لِلرَّجُلِ مِنْهُ ثَلٰثَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ قِسْمَهُ عَلَى مَازَعَمَ عَنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿatha al-wālī akhadha al-māla wa-aʿṭā li-al-rajuli minhu thalāthata ālāfi dirhamin qismahu ʿalā mā zaʿama ʿanhum
sentences.l: So sent the-governor; he-took the-money and gave to-the-man from-it three thousands of-dirham, his-portion, according-to what he-claimed from-them.
sentences.i: So the governor sent for it, took the money, and gave the man three thousand dirhams of it as his share, according to what he claimed from them,
sentences.n: فَبَعَثَ الْوَالِي أَخَذَ الْمَالَ has no connective between "sent" and "took": either a فَـ has dropped out or an object ("sent someone") is missing. I take the governor as the subject throughout. أَعْطَى لِـ "give to" with لِلرَّجُلِ is a looser construction than Classical's direct object. مَازَعَمَ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَ الْبَاقِيَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadha al-bāqiya
sentences.l: and took the-remainder.
sentences.i: and took the rest.

sentences.t: وَنَفَى الْوَالِي الثَّلٰثَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-nafā al-wālī al-thalāthata
sentences.l: And banished the-governor the-three.
sentences.i: and he banished the other three.
sentences.n: نَفَى is "to banish, send into exile". الثَّلٰثَةَ (dagger alif added, as above) are the man's three companions.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَحِقْتُ أَخِي وَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ حَالِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kharajtu anā yā amīra al-muʾminīna wa-laḥiqtu akhī wa-saʾaltuhu ʿan ḥālihi
sentences.l: And I-went-out, I, O commander-of-the-believers, and I-caught-up-with my-brother and I-asked-him about his-state.
sentences.i: I came out, Commander of the Faithful, caught up with my brother, and asked him how he was,
sentences.n: أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ is printed as one word. The speaker addresses the caliph, whom he is telling the tale. In this passage "my brother" shifts between persons, so follow each sentence on its own. لَحِقَ is "to overtake, catch up with".

sentences.t: فَأَخْبَرَنِي بِمَا ذَكَرْتُهُ لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhbaranī bi-mā dhakartuhu laka
sentences.l: and-he-informed-me with-what I-mentioned-it to-you,
sentences.i: and he told me what I have now told you,
sentences.n: أَخْبَرَ بِـ is "to inform of": the verb chooses the preposition.

sentences.t: وَأَدْخَلْتُهُ الْمَدِينَةَ سِرًّا وَرَتَّبْتُ لَهُ مَا يَأْكُلُ وَمَا يَشْرَبُ فِي الْخُفْيَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-adkhaltuhu al-madīnata sirran wa-rattabtu lahu mā yaʾkulu wa-mā yashrabu fī al-khufyati
sentences.l: and I-made-him-enter the-city secretly, and I-arranged for-him what he-eats and what he-drinks in the-secrecy.
sentences.i: I brought him into the city in secret and arranged for him, in hiding, what he should eat and drink.
sentences.n: فِي الْخُفْيَةِ, "in the secrecy", for Classical خُفْيَةً.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ حِكَايَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-khalīfatu min ḥikāyatī
sentences.l: And laughed the-caliph at my-tale.
sentences.i: The caliph laughed at my tale

sentences.t: وَقَالَ أَعْطُوهُ جَائِزَةً وَدَعُوهُ يَنْصَرِفْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla aʿṭūhu jāʾizatan wa-daʿūhu yanṣarif
sentences.l: and said: Give-him a-gift, and leave-him: let-him-depart.
sentences.i: and said, "Give him a reward and let him go."

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ مَا آخُذُ شَيْأً حَتَّى أُبَيِّنَ لِأَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَا جَرَى لِإِخْوَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu wa-Allāhi mā ākhudhu shayʾan ḥattā ubayyina li-amīri al-muʾminīna mā jarā li-ikhwatī
sentences.l: And I-said to-him: By-God I-do-not-take anything until I-make-clear to-the-commander-of-the-believers what happened to-my-brothers,
sentences.i: I said to him, "By God, I will take nothing until I have told the Commander of the Faithful what happened to my brothers,
sentences.n: The print joins لأمير المؤمنين into one word. وَاللَّهِ is an oath: وَ "by" with God in the genitive. شَيْأً is printed شيأ with the precomposed أ, which I keep.

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي قَلِيلُ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-innī qalīlu al-kalāmi
sentences.l: for I (am) few (of) the-speech.
sentences.i: for I am a man of few words."
sentences.n: This is the barber's boast, and it is ironical: in this cycle of tales he is famous for talking without end.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ وَأَمَّا أَخِي الرَّابِعُ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَهُوَ الْأَعْوَرُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla wa-ammā akhī al-rābiʿu yā amīra al-muʾminīna wa-huwa al-aʿwaru
sentences.l: Then he-said: And as-for my-brother the-fourth, O commander-of-the-believers, and he (is) the-one-eyed,
sentences.i: Then he said, "As for my fourth brother, Commander of the Faithful, the one-eyed man,
sentences.n: The telling slips from "I said" to "he said" for the same speaker, the barber; the print does not mark the change.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ جَزَّارًا بِبَغْدَادَ يَبِيعُ اللَّحْمَ وَيُرَبِّي الْكِبَاشَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu kāna jazzāran bi-baghdāda yabīʿu al-laḥma wa-yurabbī al-kibāsha
sentences.l: then-indeed-he was a-butcher in-Baghdad, selling the-meat and raising the-rams.
sentences.i: he was a butcher in Baghdad, selling meat and raising rams.
sentences.n: فَإِنَّهُ: after وَأَمَّا the sentence's main clause must begin with فَـ; here it opens the predicate. بِبَغْدَادَ: بِـ is "in" with a place name.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ يَقْصِدُونَهُ الْكِبَارُ وَأَصْحَابُ الْأَمْوَالِ يَشْتَرُونَ مِنْهُ اللَّحْمَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna yaqṣidūnahu al-kibāru wa-aṣḥābu al-amwāli yashtarūna minhu al-laḥma
sentences.l: And was they-seek-him, the-great-ones and the-owners (of) the-wealths, they-buy from-him the-meat.
sentences.i: The great men and the men of wealth used to seek him out, buying their meat from him,
sentences.n: كَانَ يَقْصِدُونَهُ: a singular كَانَ before a plural verb whose subject follows (الْكِبَارُ). This is a Middle Arabic habit, and it recurs; follow the meaning, "they used to seek him out". مِنْهُ with اِشْتَرَى is "from him".

sentences.t: فَكَسَبَ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ مَالًا عَظِيمًا وَاقْتَنَى الدَّوَابَّ وَالدُّورَ وَأَقَامَ عَلَى ذٰلِكَ زَمَنًا طَوِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-kasaba min dhālika mālan ʿaẓīman wa-iqtanā al-dawābba wa-al-dūra wa-aqāma ʿalā dhālika zamanan ṭawīlan
sentences.l: So he-earned from that wealth great, and acquired the-beasts and the-houses, and stayed on that a-time long.
sentences.i: From this he earned great wealth, acquired beasts and houses, and kept on like that for a long time.
sentences.n: الدَّوَابَّ are riding and pack animals; الدُّورَ are houses. أَقَامَ عَلَى is "to persist in, carry on with".

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَذَاتَ يَوْمٍ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ عِنْدَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwadhāta yawmin min baʿḍi al-ayyāmi ʿinda
sentences.l: Then while he, one day, from some of-the-days, at
sentences.i: Then one day, on one of those days, while he was at
sentences.n: The slice stops here, in the middle of the sentence; the next piece continues it. هُوَذَاتَ is printed as one word, هُوَ + ذَاتَ; ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ is "one day".

sentences.t: دُكَّانِهِ إِذْوَقَفَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْخٌ كَبِيرُ اللِّحْيَةِ فَدَفَعَ لَهُ دَرَاهِمَ وَقَالَ أَعْطِنِي بِهَا لَحْمًا
sentences.tr: dukkānihi idhwaqafa ʿalayhi shaykhun kabīru al-liḥyati fa-dafaʿa lahu darāhima wa-qāla aʿṭinī bihā laḥman
sentences.l: his-shop, when stood upon-him an-old-man, great-of-the-beard; and-he-paid to-him dirhams and-said: Give-me, with-them, meat.
sentences.i: his shop, when an old man with a great beard came and stood before him, handed him some dirhams, and said, "Give me meat for these."
sentences.n: This slice opens in the middle of a sentence: دُكَّانِهِ is the tail of a phrase such as "in his shop", governed by words in the previous slice. The narrator is still the barber, speaking of his brother. إِذْوَقَفَ is two words printed as one, إِذْ وَقَفَ ("when there stood"); the verb وَقَفَ عَلَيْهِ means "stand over someone", here a customer stopping at the counter.

sentences.t: وَدَفَعَ لَهُ الدَّرَاهِمَ وَانْصَرَفَ وَأَعْطَاهُ اللَّحْمَ
sentences.tr: wa-dafaʿa lahu al-darāhima wa-inṣarafa wa-aʿṭāhu al-laḥma
sentences.l: And-he-paid to-him the-dirhams, and-went-away, and-he-gave-him the-meat.
sentences.i: He paid him the coins, and the old man went off with the meat.
sentences.n: The subject changes without warning: the first and third verbs belong to the old man and to the butcher, but the print marks nothing. وَدَفَعَ repeats the payment already told, a loose, spoken way of going back over the sale. The old man's departure (وَانْصَرَفَ) is the only action of his own here.

sentences.t: فَتَأَمَّلَ أَخِي فِي فِضَّةِ الشَّيْخِ فَرَأَى دَرَاهِمَهُ بَيَاضُهَا سَاطِعٌ
sentences.tr: fa-taʾammala akhī fī fiḍḍati al-shaykhi fa-raʾā darāhimahu bayāḍuhā sāṭiʿun
sentences.l: And-he-looked-closely, my-brother, at the-silver of-the-old-man, and-saw his-dirhams, their-whiteness (being) dazzling.
sentences.i: My brother looked closely at the old man's silver and saw that the coins were dazzlingly white.
sentences.n: The final clause بَيَاضُهَا سَاطِعٌ ("their whiteness dazzling") has no linking word; it simply stands beside the object, the kind of attachment Middle Arabic uses where Classical would add a participle or a clause with أَنَّ. The print gives فَرأى with its own precomposed hamza, so that hamza is the edition's.

sentences.t: فَعَزَلَهَا فِي نَاحِيَةٍ وَحْدَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿazalahā fī nāḥiyatin waḥdahā
sentences.l: And-he-set-them-apart in a-side, alone-by-itself.
sentences.i: He put them aside in a corner by themselves.
sentences.n: وَحْدَهَا is an accusative of state, "alone", agreeing with the feminine plural dirhams as a feminine singular, as Arabic does with things.

sentences.t: وَأَقَامَ الشَّيْخُ يَتَرَدَّدُ عَلَيْهِ خَمْسَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَأَخِي يَطْرَحُ دَرَاهِمَهُ فِي صُنْدُوقٍ وَحْدَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-aqāma al-shaykhu yataraddadu ʿalayhi khamsata ashhurin wa-akhī yaṭraḥu darāhimahu fī ṣundūqin waḥdahā
sentences.l: And-remained the-old-man going-back-and-forth upon-him five months, and-my-brother throws his-dirhams into a-chest, alone-by-themselves.
sentences.i: The old man went on coming back to him for five months, while my brother kept throwing the coins into a chest of their own.
sentences.n: أَقَامَ plus a present verb ("stay, keep on doing") is a common way to say "he kept on". يَتَرَدَّدُ عَلَيْهِ is "to come to and fro", "to be a regular" at someone's shop. The present يَطْرَحُ in a story of past events gives a vivid, repeated action.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُخْرِجَهَا وَيَشْتَرِيَ غَنَمًا فَفَتَحَ الصُّنْدُوقَ فَرَأَى جَمِيعَ مَا فِيهِ وَرَقٌ أَبْيَضُ مُقَصَّصٌ
sentences.tr: thumma arāda an yukhrijahā wa-yashtariya ghanaman fa-fataḥa al-ṣundūqa fa-raʾā jamīʿa mā fīhi waraqun abyaḍu muqaṣṣaṣun
sentences.l: Then he-wanted that he-bring-them-out and-buy sheep; and-he-opened the-chest and-saw all-of what (was) in-it: paper, white, cut-up.
sentences.i: Then he decided to take them out and buy sheep with them. He opened the chest and found that everything in it was white paper, cut into scraps.
sentences.n: After فَرَأَى the Classical language would put the contents in the accusative (وَرَقًا أَبْيَضَ مُقَصَّصًا). The print leaves it bare, so I read a plain nominal clause, "all that was in it: white paper, cut up". If you prefer the accusative, only the vowel endings change. غَنَمًا is "sheep and goats", small livestock as a collective.

sentences.t: فَلَطَمَ وَجْهَهُ وَصَاحَ فَاجْتَمَعَ النَّاسُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-laṭama wajhahu wa-ṣāḥa fa-ijtamaʿa al-nāsu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-he-slapped his-face and-cried-out, and-gathered the-people upon-him.
sentences.i: He slapped his face and cried out, and people gathered around him.
sentences.n: The slap to the face is the usual gesture of grief or dismay.

sentences.t: فَحَدَّثَهُمْ بِحَدِيثِهِ فَتَعَجَّبُوا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaddathahum bi-ḥadīthihi fa-taʿajjabū minhu
sentences.l: And-he-told-them with-his-story, and-they-marvelled at-it.
sentences.i: He told them what had happened to him, and they marvelled at it.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ أَخِي عَلَى عَادَتِهِ فَذَبَحَ كَبْشًا وَعَلَّقَهُ دَاخِلَ الدُّكَّانِ وَقَطَعَ لَحْمًا وَعَلَّقَهُ خَارِجَ الدُّكَّانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma akhī ʿalā ʿādatihi fa-dhabaḥa kabshan wa-ʿallaqahu dākhila al-dukkāni wa-qaṭaʿa laḥman wa-ʿallaqahu khārija al-dukkāni
sentences.l: And-rose my-brother upon his-custom, and-he-slaughtered a-ram and-hung-it inside the-shop, and-cut meat and-hung-it outside the-shop.
sentences.i: My brother went back to his old routine. He slaughtered a ram and hung it inside the shop, then cut up some meat and hung that outside.
sentences.n: قَامَ عَلَى عَادَتِهِ, "he rose upon his custom", means he resumed his usual way of doing things. دَاخِلَ and خَارِجَ are accusatives of place, "inside" and "outside" the shop.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ أَخِي يَقُولُ يَا اللَّهُ يَجِيئُ الشَّيْخُ النَّحْسُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra akhī yaqūlu yā Allāhu yajīʾu al-shaykhu al-naḥsu
sentences.l: And-became my-brother saying: O God! comes the-old-man, the-ill-omened.
sentences.i: My brother kept saying, "O God, let that ill-omened old man come!"
sentences.n: صَارَ plus a present verb means "he went on doing, he took to doing". يَجِيئُ is printed with the precomposed hamza-seat ئ. Read it as a wish, "may he come"; Classical would use the jussive يَجِئْ, but the print keeps the full spoken form. The wish is the brother's plan: he wants the old man back so he can seize him.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَتْ سَاعَةٌ إِلَّا وَقَدْ أَقْبَلَ الشَّيْخُ وَمَعَهُ الْفِضَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kānat sāʿatun illā wa-qad aqbala al-shaykhu wa-maʿahu al-fiḍḍatu
sentences.l: And-not was an-hour except and-had approached the-old-man, and-with-him the-silver.
sentences.i: Within the hour the old man came up, with the silver in his hand.
sentences.n: مَا كَانَتْ سَاعَةٌ إِلَّا وَقَدْ… is a formula, "hardly an hour passed but"; it means it all happened very soon. سَاعَةٌ is "a short while" as often as "an hour".

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَخِي وَتَعَلَّقَ بِهِ وَصَارَ يَزْعَقُ يَا مُسْلِمِينَ اِلْحَقُونِي وَاسْمَعُوا قِصَّتِي مَعَ هَذَا الْفَاجِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma akhī wa-taʿallaqa bihi wa-ṣāra yazʿaqu yā muslimīna ilḥaqūnī wa-asmaʿū qiṣṣatī maʿa hādhā al-fājiri
sentences.l: And-rose my-brother and-clung to-him, and-began shouting: O Muslims! come-to-my-aid, and-hear my-story with this wicked-one!
sentences.i: My brother jumped up, seized hold of him, and started shouting, "Muslims, help me! Listen to what this scoundrel has done to me!"
sentences.n: يَزْعَقُ "to shout" is a word of the spoken language. يَا مُسْلِمِينَ keeps the oblique ending in the vocative, as is common in this text. اِلْحَقُونِي is "catch up with me", i.e. "come to my rescue". تَعَلَّقَ بِهِ is "cling to him", the grip of a man who will not let go.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشَّيْخُ كَلَامَهُ قَالَ لَهُ الشَّيْخُ أَيُّمَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ تَتَنَحَّى عَنِّي أَوْ أَفْضَحُكَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shaykhu kalāmahu qāla lahu al-shaykhu ayyumā aḥabbu ilayka tatanaḥḥā ʿannī aw afḍaḥuka bayna al-nāsi
sentences.l: And-when heard the-old-man his-speech, said to-him the-old-man: Which (is) dearer to-you: you-move-aside from-me, or I-expose-you among the-people?
sentences.i: When the old man heard this, he said to him, "Which would you rather: that you get away from me, or that I shame you in front of everyone?"
sentences.n: أَيُّمَا is أَيُّ "which" with the extra مَا that Middle Arabic likes. The two options are set side by side with no أَنْ ("that") in front of them, and I read the second verb as indicative أَفْضَحُكَ, as the print leaves it open. فَضَحَ is to expose to public shame.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي بِأَيِّ شَيُّ تَفْضَحُنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī bi-ayyi shayyin tafḍaḥunī
sentences.l: And-said to-him my-brother: With what thing will-you-expose-me?
sentences.i: My brother said to him, "Shame me with what?"
sentences.n: The print puts a damma on the last letter of شَيُّ, one of the few marks the edition adds in prose, so I keep it. The word is the spoken شَيّ for شَيْء, "thing"; after بِأَيِّ one would expect a genitive ending, so the damma looks like a stray mark. بِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ is "on what ground" more than "with what".

sentences.t: قَالَ بِأَنَّكَ تَبِيعُ لَحْمَ النَّاسِ بِأَنَّهُ لَحْمُ غَنَمٍ
sentences.tr: qāla bi-annaka tabīʿu laḥma al-nāsi bi-annahu laḥmu ghanamin
sentences.l: He-said: With-that-you sell the-flesh of-people with-that-it (is) the-flesh of-sheep.
sentences.i: He said, "With the fact that you sell human flesh and pass it off as mutton."
sentences.n: The first بِـ answers the question ("with what?": "with this, that you sell…"). The second بِـ in بِأَنَّهُ introduces the label under which the meat is sold, "as being"; the next unit says the same with عَلَى أَنَّهُ. لَحْمَ النَّاسِ is "people-flesh": the charge is cannibal butchery, said plainly.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي كَذَبْتَ يَا مَلْعُونُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī kadhabta yā malʿūnu
sentences.l: And-said to-him my-brother: You-lied, O cursed-one!
sentences.i: My brother said to him, "You lie, you cursed man!"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ مَا مَلْعُونٌ إِلَّا الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ رَجُلٌ فِى الدُّكَّانِ مُعَلَّقٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu mā malʿūnun illā al-ladhī ʿindahu rajulun fī al-dukkāni muʿallaqun
sentences.l: And-said the-old-man: Not (is) cursed except the-one-who with-him (is) a-man in the-shop, hung.
sentences.i: The old man said, "The only cursed man is the one who has a man hanging in his shop."
sentences.n: فِى is printed with the dotless final ى, a spelling habit of the edition that I keep. The adjective مُعَلَّقٌ comes last, after the phrase فِى الدُّكَّانِ; the word order is loose, "a man in the shop, hanging".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي إِنْ كَانَ الْأَمْرُ كَمَا ذَكَرْتَ فَمَالِى وَدَمِي حَلَالٌ لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī in kāna al-amru ka-mā dhakarta fa-mālī wa-damī ḥalālun laka
sentences.l: And-said to-him my-brother: If the-matter is as you-mentioned, then my-wealth and-my-blood (are) lawful to-you.
sentences.i: My brother said to him, "If it is as you say, then my property and my life are yours to take."
sentences.n: كَمَا ذَكَرْتَ is "just as you mentioned", with كَـ "as" and مَا "what". مَالِى وَدَمِي حَلَالٌ لَكَ is the strong formula of surrender: "my wealth and my blood are lawful to you", meaning you may take both. The verb إِنْ كَانَ is past in form but conditional in sense. مَالِى is printed with ى, as in the print.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ يَا مَعَاشِرَ النَّاسِ إِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ تَحْقِيقَ قَوْلِي وَصِدْقِي اُدْخُلُوا دُكَّانَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu yā maʿāshira al-nāsi in aradtum taḥqīqa qawlī wa-ṣidqī udkhulū dukkānahu
sentences.l: And-said the-old-man: O companies of-people, if you-wish the-verification of-my-word and-my-truthfulness, enter his-shop.
sentences.i: The old man said, "People, if you want proof that I am telling the truth, go into his shop."
sentences.n: يَا مَعَاشِرَ النَّاسِ is a rhetorical address, "O assembled people" (مَعَاشِر is the plural of مَعْشَر, a company or band).

sentences.t: فَهَجَمَ النَّاسُ عَلَى دُكَّانِ أَخِي فَرَأَوْا ذَلِكَ الْكَبْشَ صَارَ إِنْسَانًا مُعَلَّقًا
sentences.tr: fa-hajama al-nāsu ʿalā dukkāni akhī fa-raʾaw dhālika al-kabsha ṣāra insānan muʿallaqan
sentences.l: And-rushed the-people upon the-shop of-my-brother, and-they-saw that ram, it-had-become a-man, hung.
sentences.i: The crowd rushed into my brother's shop and saw that the ram had turned into a man, hanging there.
sentences.n: This is the sorcery of the tale: the old man's silver turned to paper, and now the ram turns into a man. The verb صَارَ stands right after the object without any linking word, "they saw the ram: it had become a man", and I translate the sense.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا ذَلِكَ تَعَلَّقُوا بِأَخِي وَصَاحُوا عَلَيْهِ يَا كَافِرِيَا فَاجِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaw dhālika taʿallaqū bi-akhī wa-ṣāḥū ʿalayhi yā kāfiri yā fājiru
sentences.l: And-when they-saw that, they-clung to-my-brother and-cried at-him: O unbeliever, O wicked-one!
sentences.i: When they saw it, they seized my brother and shouted at him, "You infidel! You scoundrel!"
sentences.n: The print runs يَا كَافِر يَا فَاجِر together as يَا كَافِرِيَا فَاجِر: the second يَا is glued onto كَافِر. I vocalise the letters as printed and read it as two vocatives, "O unbeliever, O wicked one". The two cries are two stock insults.

sentences.t: وَصَارَا عَزُّ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ يَضْرِبُهُ وَيَلْطِمُهُ وَيَقُولُ لَهُ أَنْتَ تُطْعِمُنَا لَحْمَ بَنِي آدَمَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra aʿazzu al-nāsi ilayhi yaḍribuhu wa-yalṭimuhu wa-yaqūlu lahu anta tuṭʿimunā laḥma banī ādama
sentences.l: And-became (the) dearest of-the-people to-him beating-him and-slapping-him and-saying to-him: You, you-feed-us the-flesh of-the-sons of-Adam!
sentences.i: And the very people dearest to him began to beat him and slap him, saying, "You feed us human flesh!"
sentences.n: Word-division oddity: the print has وَصَارَا عَزّ, with the alif of أَعَزّ attached to the end of صَارَ. The sense is وَصَارَ أَعَزُّ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ, "and the dearest of people to him began…", meaning those closest to the brother joined in beating him. I keep the letters as printed and show the true division in the transliteration. The singular verbs يَضْرِبُهُ… agree with the singular أَعَزُّ. بَنِي آدَمَ "sons of Adam" is the common phrase for human beings; the print gives آدَمَ with its own precomposed madda.

sentences.t: وَلَطَمَهُ الشَّيْخُ عَلَى عَيْنِهِ قَلَعَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-laṭamahu al-shaykhu ʿalā ʿaynihi qalaʿahā
sentences.l: And-slapped-him the-old-man upon his-eye, he-tore-it-out.
sentences.i: And the old man struck him on the eye and knocked it clean out.
sentences.n: The two verbs are set side by side without a conjunction: the blow, then the result. قَلَعَ is "to tear out, uproot"; the Arabic is blunt and I keep it so.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلَتِ النَّاسُ ذَلِكَ الْمَذْبُوحَ إِلَى صَاحِبِ الشُّرْطَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamalati al-nāsu dhālika al-madhbūḥa ilā ṣāḥibi al-shurṭati
sentences.l: And-carried (f.) the-people that slaughtered-one to the-master of-the-police.
sentences.i: The crowd carried the slaughtered man to the chief of police.
sentences.n: The verb is feminine singular (حَمَلَتِ) though the subject النَّاسُ is grammatically masculine; Middle Arabic treats a collective as feminine, and the spoken language does this all the time. الْمَذْبُوح is "the slaughtered one": the carcass, which they take for a human victim. صَاحِبُ الشُّرْطَةِ is the officer in charge of the city's police and justice.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّيْخُ أَيُّهَا الْأَمِيرُ هَذَا الرَّجُلُ يَذْبَحُ النَّاسَ وَيَبِيعُ لَحْمَهُمْ عَلَى أَنَّهُ لَحْمُ غَنَمٍ وَقَدْ أَتَيْنَاكَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-shaykhu ayyuhā al-amīru hādhā al-rajulu yadhbaḥu al-nāsa wa-yabīʿu laḥmahum ʿalā annahu laḥmu ghanamin wa-qad atynāka bihi
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-old-man: O emir, this man slaughters the-people and-sells their-flesh on (the claim) that-it (is) the-flesh of-sheep; and indeed we-have-come-to-you with-him.
sentences.i: The old man said to him, "Emir, this man slaughters people and sells their flesh as mutton, and we have brought him to you."
sentences.n: عَلَى أَنَّهُ means "on the basis that, passing it off as". أَتَيْنَاكَ بِهِ is "we have come to you with him", i.e. "we have brought him to you": the verb أَتَى takes بِـ for the thing brought.

sentences.t: فَقُمْ وَاقْضِ حَقَّ اللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qum wa-iqḍi ḥaqqa Allāhi ʿazza wa-jalla
sentences.l: So rise and-judge the-right of-God, mighty-and-exalted.
sentences.i: "So rise, and do the justice that God, great and glorious, demands."
sentences.n: عَزَّوَجَلَّ is printed as one word, عَزَّ وَجَلَّ, the formula "mighty and exalted" said after God's name. اِقْضِ حَقَّ اللَّهِ is "pass judgment on what is due to God", a request for the law's penalty.

sentences.t: فَدَافَعَ أَخِي عَنْ نَفْسِهِ فَلَمْ يَسْمَعْ مِنْهُ وَأَمَرَ بِضَرْبِهِ خَمْسَمِائَةِ عَصًا
sentences.tr: fa-dāfaʿa akhī ʿan nafsihi fa-lam yasmaʿ minhu wa-amara bi-ḍarbihi khamsamiʾati ʿaṣan
sentences.l: And-defended my-brother from himself, and-he-did-not hear from-him, and-ordered with-the-striking-of-him five-hundred of-stick.
sentences.i: My brother pleaded in his own defence, but the emir would not listen to him and ordered that he be given five hundred strokes with a stick.
sentences.n: فَلَمْ يَسْمَعْ مِنْهُ: the subject is the emir, who "did not hear from him". أَمَرَ بِـ is the verb with its own preposition, "to order (something)": here أَمَرَ بِضَرْبِهِ, "he ordered his beating". خَمْسَمِائَةِ is printed as one word, with the edition's own precomposed ئ. عَصًا is an accusative of specification ("five hundred, of staff").

sentences.t: وَأَخَذُوا جَمِيعَ مَالِهِ وَلَوْلَا الْمَالُ لَقَتَلُوهُ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhū jamīʿa mālihi wa-law-lā al-mālu la-qatalūhu
sentences.l: And-they-took all (of) his-wealth; and-if-not (for) the-wealth, they-would-have-killed-him.
sentences.i: They also took all his money, and if it had not been for the money, they would have killed him.
sentences.n: وَلَوْلَا الْمَالُ لَقَتَلُوهُ: with لَوْلَا the reason is in the nominative and the answer takes لَـ, "had it not been for the money, they would have killed him". The sense is that the money bought his life.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَخِي هَا جَا عَلَى رَأْسِهِ حَتَّى دَخَلَ مَدِينَةً كَبِيرَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāma akhī hā jā ʿalā raʾsihi ḥattā dakhala madīnatan kabīratan
sentences.l: And-rose my-brother, hā-jā(?) (perhaps hāʾijan, "frantic"), upon his-head, until he-entered a-city, big.
sentences.i: My brother got up and wandered off, dazed, until he came to a large city.
sentences.n: Obscure. The print has two small words, هَا جَا, before عَلَى رَأْسِهِ. They may be a mis-spaced هَائِجًا ("frantic", from هَاجَ "to be stirred up"); the sense, "went off on his head" or "headlong", is the same either way. I keep the letters and translate the sense, "dazed" or "headlong". The print has رَأْسِهِ with its own precomposed hamza.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَحْسَنَ لَهُ أَنْ يَعْمَلَ إِسْكَافِيًّا فَفَتَحَ دُكَّانًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna aḥsana lahu an yaʿmala iskāfiyyan fa-fataḥa dukkānan
sentences.l: And-it-was best for-him that he-work (as) a-cobbler; so-he-opened a-shop.
sentences.i: He thought it best to work as a cobbler, and so he opened a shop.
sentences.n: كَانَ أَحْسَنَ لَهُ أَنْ… is "it was best for him to…", with the clause as the subject of كَانَ and أَحْسَنَ as its predicate. It states his decision in the form of a judgment. إِسْكَافِيّ is a cobbler or shoemaker.

sentences.t: وَقَعَدَ يَعْمَلُ شَيْأً يَتَقَوَّتُ بِهِ
