sentences.tr: wa-qaʿada yaʿmalu shayʾan yataqawwatu bihi
sentences.l: And-he-sat working a-thing; he-sustains-himself with-it.
sentences.i: He sat down to some work that would keep him alive.
sentences.n: قَعَدَ plus a present verb ("sat doing") means he settled down to the work. يَتَقَوَّتُ بِهِ is "to live on it, to get one's daily bread by it"; the verb takes بِـ for the means. شَيْأً is printed with the edition's own precomposed أ.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ فِي حَاجَةٍ فَسَمِعَ حِسَّ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja dhāta yawmin fī ḥājatin fa-samiʿa ḥissa
sentences.l: And-he-went-out one day on a-need, and-heard the-sound of —
sentences.i: One day he went out on an errand and heard a sound...
sentences.n: The slice ends here, mid-sentence: حِسَّ is the first word of a phrase like "the sound of…" that the next slice completes. ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ is "one day" (literally "the self of a day"); فِي حَاجَةٍ is "on some business".

sentences.t: خَيْلٌ فَسَأَلَ عَنْ ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: khaylun fa-saʾala ʿan dhālika
sentences.l: Horse(s); and he asked about that.
sentences.i: ...horsemen; so he asked about it,
sentences.n: The slice opens in the middle of a sentence: خَيْلٌ ("horse, horsemen") depends on a verb (probably "he saw") in the previous passage, so its case here is only a guess. ذٰلِكَ is printed ذلك, without the long ā, so it is pointed with a dagger alif (ٰ).

sentences.t: فَقِيلَ لَهُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ خَارِجٌ فِى الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ
sentences.tr: fa-qīla lahu anna al-malika khārijun fī al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi
sentences.l: And it-was-said to-him that the king (is) going-out in the hunting and the chase.
sentences.i: and was told that the king was out hunting and coursing.
sentences.n: The print writes فى with a final ى, and so does the pointing. خَارِج is "going out, out and about". الصَّيْد and الْقَنْص are near-synonyms (hunting, game-chase), paired as the Arabic likes.

sentences.t: فَجَعَلَ أَخِي يَنْظُرُ إِلَى حُسْنِ الْمَلِكِ فَوَقَعَتْ عَيْنُ الْمَلِكِ فِي عَيْنِ أَخِي
sentences.tr: fa-jaʿala akhī yanẓuru ilā ḥusni al-maliki fa-waqaʿat ʿaynu al-maliki fī ʿayni akhī
sentences.l: And began my-brother he-looks at the beauty of-the-king, and fell the eye of-the-king in the eye of-my-brother.
sentences.i: My brother began to gaze at the splendour of the king's train, and the king's eye fell upon my brother's eye.
sentences.n: The speaker is still the barber, telling of his brother. جَعَلَ + imperfect means "began to...". حُسْن is "beauty, fine show", here the splendid look of the king and his retinue. عَيْنُ الْمَلِكِ... فِي عَيْنِ أَخِي: the two glances meet; the brother has only one eye, which is what is about to matter.

sentences.t: فَأَطْرَقَ الْمَلِكُ بِرَأْسِهِ وَقَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَرِّ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-aṭraqa al-maliku bi-raʾsihi wa-qāla aʿūdhu bi-Allāhi min sharri hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: And bowed the king with his-head, and said: I-seek-refuge with God from the evil of this day.
sentences.i: The king lowered his head and said, "I take refuge with God from the evil of this day!"
sentences.n: أَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ is "to lower the head, look down". The print gives رأسه with its hamza already written, so it is kept as printed. The king's cry shows the belief that the sight of a one-eyed man in the morning brings bad luck.

sentences.t: وَاثْنَى عِنَانَ فَرَسِهِ وَرَجَعَ فَرَجَعَ جَمِيعُ الْغِلْمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ithnā ʿināna farasihi wa-rajaʿa fa-rajaʿa jamīʿu al-ghilmāni
sentences.l: And he-turned the rein of-his-horse and returned; so returned all the lads.
sentences.i: He turned his horse's head and rode back, and all his servants rode back with him.
sentences.n: وَاثْنَى is the print's spelling; the Classical verb is ثَنَى ("to turn, bend back"), and this form with a prefixed alif is the print's own (compare اِنْثَنَى). I point it as printed. The sentence began on the previous line and ends at the second رَجَعَ, which is the servants' response. الْغِلْمَان is the Middle Arabic plural of غُلَام, "lad, servant".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ الْغِلْمَانَ فَلَحِقُوا أَخِي فَضَرَبُوهُ ضَرْبًا وَجِيعًا حَتَّى كَادَ أَنْ يَمُوتَ
sentences.tr: thumma amara al-ghilmāna fa-laḥiqū akhī fa-ḍarabūhu ḍarban wajīʿan ḥattā kāda an yamūta
sentences.l: Then he-ordered the lads, and they-overtook my-brother and struck-him a-striking painful until he-nearly that he-die.
sentences.i: Then he ordered his servants, and they caught up with my brother and beat him savagely, until he was nearly dead.
sentences.n: كَادَ أَنْ يَمُوتَ keeps the أَنْ that Classical Arabic usually omits after كَادَ; this is common in later texts. ضَرْبًا وَجِيعًا is an internal object ("a striking, a painful one"). Note that the king's servants give no reason: the beating is for the one-eyed man's ill omen.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَدْرِ أَخِي مَا السَّبَبُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yadri akhī mā al-sababu
sentences.l: And did-not know my-brother what (was) the cause.
sentences.i: My brother had no idea why.

sentences.t: فَرَجَعَ إِلَى مَوْضِعِهِ وَهُوَ فِي حَالَةِ الْعَدَمِ
sentences.tr: fa-rajaʿa ilā mawḍiʿihi wa-huwa fī ḥālati al-ʿadami
sentences.l: So he-returned to his-place, and he in the state of-the-non-being.
sentences.i: So he went back to his lodging, in a state of utter wretchedness.
sentences.n: الْعَدَم is "non-existence, lack"; حَالَة الْعَدَم suggests either destitution or being wiped out, beside oneself. I take it as total wretchedness, which suits both a beaten and a baffled man. The print writes في here, with ي.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَضَى إِلَى إِنْسَانٍ مِنْ حَاشِيَةِ الْمَلِكِ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ مَا وَقَعَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma maḍā ilā insānin min ḥāshiyati al-maliki wa-qaṣṣa ʿalayhi mā waqaʿa lahu
sentences.l: Then he-went to a-person from the retinue of-the-king, and related to-him what had-befallen to-him.
sentences.i: Then he went to a man of the king's household and told him what had happened to him.
sentences.n: إِنْسَان is used loosely for "a person, someone". حَاشِيَة is the entourage, the people at the edge (حَاشِيَة, "margin") of the king. قَصَّ عَلَيْهِ is "to recount to someone", the verb for telling a story.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ حَتَّى اسْتَلْقَى عَلَى قَفَاهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika ḥattā istalqā ʿalā qafāhu wa-qāla lahu yā akhī
sentences.l: And he-laughed until he-lay-back on his-nape, and said to-him: O my-brother,
sentences.i: The man laughed until he fell over backwards, and said to him, "My brother,
sentences.n: اسْتَلْقَى عَلَى قَفَاهُ is "to throw oneself on one's back": he rolled with laughter.

sentences.t: اعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ لَا يُطِيقُ أَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلَى أَعْوَرَ لَا سِيَّمَا إِنْكَانَ أَعْوَرَ بِالْيُمْنَى
sentences.tr: iʿlam anna al-malika lā yuṭīqu an yanẓura ilā aʿwara lā siyyamā inkāna aʿwara bi-al-yumnā
sentences.l: Know that the king not he-can-bear that he-look at a-one-eyed-man, not like-unto-it if-he-was one-eyed in-the-right.
sentences.i: know that the king cannot bear to look at a one-eyed man, least of all one who is blind in the right eye,
sentences.n: The print writes انكان as one word, "if he was" (إِنْ كَانَ); I keep it joined and point it إِنْكَانَ. لَا سِيَّمَا is printed as two words, "above all". بِالْيُمْنَى: the right (eye); the بِـ is the "in" of a respect, "one-eyed in the right". أَعْوَر is one-eyed, here a diptote (no tanwīn). The speaker's grammar is Classical and the matter is only the superstition.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ لَا يُعْتِقُهُ دُونَ قَتْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu lā yuʿtiquhu dūna qatlihi
sentences.l: For he not he-frees-him short-of killing-him.
sentences.i: for he will not let him go without killing him."
sentences.n: يُعْتِقُ is properly "to set free"; here it means "let off, let go". دُونَ قَتْلِهِ is "short of his killing", i.e. "without having him killed".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَخِي ذٰلِكَ الْكَلَامَ عَزَمَ عَلَى الْهُرُوبِ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa akhī dhālika al-kalāma ʿazama ʿalā al-hurūbi min tilka al-madīnati
sentences.l: And when heard my-brother that speech, he-resolved upon the fleeing from that city.
sentences.i: When my brother heard this, he resolved to flee from that city.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَ وَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا وَتَحَوَّلَ إِلَى نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى لَمْ يَكُنْ بِهَا أَحَدٌ يَعْرِفُهُ وَأَقَامَ بِهَا زَمَنًا طَوِيلًا
sentences.tr: thumma qāma wa-kharaja minhā wa-taḥawwala ilā nāḥiyatin ukhrā lam yakun bihā aḥadun yaʿrifuhu wa-aqāma bihā zamanan ṭawīlan
sentences.l: Then he-rose and went-out from-it, and moved to a-region another, not was in-it anyone knowing-him; and he-stayed in-it a-time long.
sentences.i: Then he got up, left it, and moved to another region where nobody knew him, and he stayed there a long time.
sentences.n: لَمْ يَكُنْ بِهَا أَحَدٌ يَعْرِفُهُ is "there was not in it anyone who knew him"; the relative clause يَعْرِفُهُ has no linking word, as Arabic allows after an indefinite noun. بِهَا the first time is "in it" (the region), the second time too ("he stayed in it").

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ تَفَكَّرَ أَخِي فِي أَمْرِهِ وَخَرَجَ يَوْمًا يَتَفَرَّجُ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika tafakkara akhī fī amrihi wa-kharaja yawman yatafarraju
sentences.l: Then after that pondered my-brother on his-affair, and went-out one-day he-takes-a-stroll.
sentences.i: After that, my brother thought over his situation, and one day went out for a stroll.
sentences.n: يَتَفَرَّجُ is "to amuse oneself, go for a stroll, take the air", a word of the spoken language; it follows خَرَجَ without a linking word. يَوْمًا is "one day".

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ حِسَّ خَيْلٍ خَلْفَهُ فَقَالَ جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa ḥissa khaylin khalfahu fa-qāla jāʾa amru Allāhi
sentences.l: And he-heard the sound of-horse behind-him, and said: There-came the command of-God.
sentences.i: Then he heard the sound of horses behind him, and said, "The decree of God has come!"
sentences.n: جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ is an exclamation of resignation before disaster: "God's decree has come". حِسّ is "sound, noise".

sentences.t: فَطَلَبَ مَوْضِعًا يَسْتَتِرُ فِيهِ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaba mawḍiʿan yastatiru fīhi fa-lam yajid
sentences.l: And he-sought a-place he-hides in-it, and did-not find.
sentences.i: He looked for a place to hide in, and found none.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ فَإِذَا بِبَابٍ مَغْلُوقٍ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara fa-idhā bi-bābin maghlūqin
sentences.l: Then he-looked, and behold, a-door closed.
sentences.i: Then he looked, and behold, a closed door.
sentences.n: After إِذَا of surprise the بِـ only marks what comes into view ("and behold, a door"). مَغْلُوق is "closed"; the Middle Arabic غَلَقَ replaces Classical أَغْلَقَ.

sentences.t: فَدَفَعَ ذٰلِكَ الْبَابَ فَوَقَعَ فَدَخَلَ فَرَأَى دِهْلِيزًا طَوِيلًا فَدَخَلَ أَخِي فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-dafaʿa dhālika al-bāba fa-waqaʿa fa-dakhala fa-raʾā dihlīzan ṭawīlan fa-dakhala akhī fīhi
sentences.l: And he-pushed that door and it-fell, and he-entered, and saw a-passage long; and entered my-brother in-it.
sentences.i: He pushed the door and it fell open; he went in and saw a long passage, and my brother went along it.
sentences.n: وَقَعَ "it fell": the door gave way, flat on the ground or open. دِهْلِيز is a vestibule or passage, borrowed from Persian. The print has فراى without the hamza sign; it is رَأَى, "he saw".

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَرَجُلَانِ قَدْ تَعَلَّقَا بِهِ وَقَالَا لِأَخِى الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yashʿur illā wa-rajulāni qad taʿallaqā bihi wa-qālā li-akhī al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi
sentences.l: And he-did-not perceive but and two-men had clung to-him, and they-said to-my-brother: The praise (is) to God
sentences.i: He knew nothing more until two men had seized him, and they said to my brother, "Praise be to God
sentences.n: لَمْ يَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَ... is "he did not notice anything until, behold, ..." (a frequent narrative idiom). تَعَلَّقَ بِـ is "to cling to, grab hold of". لِأَخِى is the print's spelling (with ى) of لِأَخِي.

sentences.t: الَّذِي أَمْكَنَنَا مِنْكَ يَا عَدُ وَاللَّهِ
sentences.tr: alladhī amkananā minka yā ʿadu wa-Allāhi
sentences.l: who gave-power to-us over-you, O enemy of-God!
sentences.i: who has put you in our power, enemy of God!
sentences.n: The print divides the words wrongly: يا عد والله has the letters of يَا عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ, "O enemy of God". I keep the printed letters and division, so the word عَدُ is pointed with the construct ending and وَاللَّهِ stands for the second word with its waw, which really belongs to عَدُوّ. Read it as "yā ʿaduwwa Allāh". أَمْكَنَ مِنْ is "to give someone power over".

sentences.t: هَذِهِ ثَلٰثَ لَيَالٍ مَا خَلَّيْتَنَا نَنَامُ وَلَا نَهْدِي وَقَدْ أَذَقْتَنَا الْمَوْتَ
sentences.tr: hādhihi thalātha layālin mā khallaytanā nanāmu wa-lā nahdī wa-qad adhaqtanā al-mawta
sentences.l: These three nights not you-let-us we-sleep, nor we-rest; and you-have-made-us-taste death.
sentences.i: For three nights now you haven't let us sleep or rest, and you have made us taste death!
sentences.n: ثلث is printed for ثَلَاثَ, so it takes the dagger alif. نَنَامُ and نَهْدِي follow مَا خَلَّيْتَنَا with no أَنْ, and are indicative: Middle Arabic. نَهْدِي is the print's spelling of نَهْدَأُ, "we are calm"; the hamza has softened to ي in the speech. أَذَاقَ الْمَوْتَ "to make taste death" means to torment mightily.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي يَا قَوْمُ مَا أَمْرُكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī yā qawmu mā amrukum
sentences.l: And said my-brother: O people, what (is) your-affair?
sentences.i: My brother said, "Good people, what is the matter with you?"

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا أَنْتَ تُغِيرُ عَلَيْنَا وَتُرِيدُ تَفْضَحُنَا وَتُدَبِّرُ الْحِيلَةَ وَتُرِيدُ تَذْبَحُ صَاحِبَ الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū anta tughīru ʿalaynā wa-turīdu tafḍaḥunā wa-tudabbiru al-ḥīlata wa-turīdu tadhbaḥu ṣāḥiba al-bayti
sentences.l: And they-said: You, you-raid upon-us, and you-want you-disgrace-us, and you-plot the trick, and you-want you-slaughter the master of-the-house.
sentences.i: They said, "You come raiding us, you mean to disgrace us, you plot your trick, and you want to cut the throat of the master of the house!
sentences.n: Here the men take the stranger for a thief or assassin. تُرِيدُ تَفْضَحُنَا and تُرِيدُ تَذْبَحُ have no أَنْ between the verbs and are indicative: the usual Middle Arabic way. تُغِيرُ عَلَيْنَا is "you raid us". الْحِيلَة is a trick, a stratagem. صَاحِب الْبَيْت is the householder, the owner of the house.

sentences.t: مَا يَكْفِيكَ أَنَّكَ أَفْقَرْتَهُ وَأَصْحَابُكَ
sentences.tr: mā yakfīka annaka afqartahu wa-aṣḥābuka
sentences.l: Not it-suffices-you that-you impoverished-him, and your-companions?
sentences.i: Is it not enough that you and your companions have ruined him?
sentences.n: أَفْقَرْتَهُ وَأَصْحَابُكَ joins a noun to the "you" inside the verb, so "you and your companions impoverished him". Classical usage would add أَنْتَ before it; the print does not.

sentences.t: وَلٰكِنْ أَخْرِجْ لَنَا السِّكِّينَ الَّتِي تُهَدِّدُنَا بِهَا كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin akhrij lanā al-sikkīna allatī tuhaddidunā bihā kulla laylatin
sentences.l: But bring-out for-us the knife which you-threaten-us with-it every night.
sentences.i: Come now, hand over the knife you threaten us with every night."
sentences.n: ولكن is printed without its alif, so it is pointed وَلٰكِنْ with the dagger. السِّكِّين (knife) is feminine here, so it is followed by الَّتِي.

sentences.t: وَفَتَّشُوهُ فَوَجَدُوا فِي وَسْطِهِ سِكِّينًا
sentences.tr: wa-fattashūhu fa-wajadū fī wasṭihi sikkīnan
sentences.l: And they-searched-him, and found in his-middle a-knife.
sentences.i: They searched him and found a knife at his waist.
sentences.n: وَسْطِهِ "his middle" is the waist, where the knife was tucked in the sash.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا قَوْمُ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ فِي أَمْرِي وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ حَدِيثِي عَجِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā qawmu ittaqū Allāha fī amrī wa-iʿlamū anna ḥadīthī ʿajībun
sentences.l: And he-said: O people, fear God in my-affair, and know that my-tale (is) strange.
sentences.i: He said, "Good people, fear God in my case, and know that my story is a strange one.
sentences.n: اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ فِي is "fear God where it concerns...", an appeal to treat someone justly.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا وَمَا حَدِيثُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū wa-mā ḥadīthuka
sentences.l: And they-said: And what (is) your-tale?
sentences.i: "And what is your story?" they said.

sentences.t: فَحَدَّثَهُمْ بِحَدِيثِهِ طَمَعًا أَنْ يُطْلِقُوهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaddathahum bi-ḥadīthihi ṭamaʿan an yuṭliqūhu
sentences.l: So he-told-them with his-tale, in-hope that they-release-him.
sentences.i: So he told them his story, hoping they would let him go.
sentences.n: حَدَّثَ بِـ is "to tell someone a story": the verb takes the person as direct object and the story with بِـ. طَمَعًا is an adverbial accusative of purpose, "out of hope".

sentences.t: فَمَا سَمِعُوا مِنْ أَخِي مَا قَالَ وَلَا الْتَفَتُوا إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā samiʿū min akhī mā qāla wa-lā iltafatū ilayhi
sentences.l: But they-did-not hear from my-brother what he-said, nor did-they-turn to-him.
sentences.i: But they would not listen to a word he said, and paid him no attention.

sentences.t: وَضَرَبُوهُ وَخَرَّقُوا أَثْوَا بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḍarabūhu wa-kharraqū athwā bihi
sentences.l: And they-struck-him and tore his-garments.
sentences.i: They beat him and tore his clothes,
sentences.n: The print divides اثوابه ("his garments") into اثوا به; I keep the printed division, so أَثْوَا is the plural of ثَوْب with its last letter bare, and بِهِ is the rest. Read it as one word, athwābihi. خَرَّقَ is "to tear into pieces".

sentences.t: فَوَجَدُوا عَلَيْهِ أَثَرَ الضَّرْبِ بِالْمَقَارِعِ عَلَى أَجْنَابِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadū ʿalayhi athara al-ḍarbi bi-al-maqāriʿi ʿalā ajnābihi
sentences.l: And they-found upon-him the trace of-the-beating with-the-whips upon his-sides.
sentences.i: and found the marks of a flogging with whips along his sides.
sentences.n: The unit runs over the printed page break. الْمَقَارِع are whips (singular مِقْرَعَة), here the ones used on the brother by the king's servants. أَجْنَاب is a plural of جَنْب, "side, flank".

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهُ يَا مَلْعُونُ هَذَا أَثَرُ الضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahu yā malʿūnu hādhā atharu al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: And they-said to-him: O accursed, this (is) the trace of-the-beating!
sentences.i: They said to him, "Cursed man, here are the marks of a beating!"

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرُوا أَخِي بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الْوَالِي
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍarū akhī bayna yadayi al-wālī
sentences.l: Then they-brought my-brother between the hands of-the-governor.
sentences.i: Then they brought my brother before the governor.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيِ is "in front of"; the dual ending drops its nūn before the following word, and the kasra is only for the join to الْ. الْوَالِي is the governor, here also the chief of police.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ قَدْ وَقَعْتُ بِذُنُوبِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī nafsihi qad waqaʿtu bi-dhunūbī
sentences.l: And he-said in his-self: I-have fallen through my-sins.
sentences.i: He said to himself, "I have fallen into this because of my sins,
sentences.n: وَقَعَ بِـ is "to fall into trouble because of...". بِذُنُوبِي: the بِـ gives the cause, "by reason of my sins".

sentences.t: وَمَا يُخَلِّصُنِي إِلَّا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: wa-mā yukhalliṣunī illā Allāhu taʿālā
sentences.l: And none delivers-me except God, Exalted.
sentences.i: and none can deliver me but God Most High."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَالِي لِأَخِي يَا فَاجِرُ مَا حَمَلَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wālī li-akhī yā fājiru mā ḥamalaka
sentences.l: And said the governor to-my-brother: O wicked-one, what carried-you
sentences.i: Then the governor said to my brother, "You scoundrel, what drove you
sentences.n: The slice ends here, in the middle of the governor's question: مَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى... "what led you to...". الْفَاجِر is a debauched, wicked man, used as an insult.

sentences.t: عَلَى هَذَا الْأَمْرِ تَدْخُلُ دَارَهُمْ بِالْقَتْلِ
sentences.tr: ʿalā hādhā al-amri tadkhulu dārahum bi-al-qatli
sentences.l: On this matter you-enter their house with-the-killing?
sentences.i: to this: to force your way into their house, bent on murder?"
sentences.n: The slice opens in the middle of a speech that began on the previous page: this is the governor rebuking the brother, as the next sentences show. The sentence has no question word; the tone makes it a reproach, and عَلَى هَذَا الْأَمْرِ is best read as "for this reason, on this account".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي سَأَلْتُكَ بِاللَّهِ أَيُّهَا الْأَمِيرُ اسْمَعْ كَلَامِي وَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī saʾaltuka bi-Allāhi ayyuhā al-amīru ismaʿ kalāmī wa-lā taʿjal ʿalayya
sentences.l: And said to-him my-brother: I-asked-you by-God, O the-emir, hear my-speech and do-not hasten against-me.
sentences.i: My brother said to him, "I beg you by God, O Emir, hear what I have to say, and do not rush to judgment against me."
sentences.n: سَأَلْتُكَ بِاللَّهِ ("I asked you by God") is a set formula of appeal, with the perfect used for a present plea. عَجِلَ عَلَى is "to hurry against", that is, to act hastily to someone's harm.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَالِي نَسْمَعُ كَلَامَ لِصٍّ قَدْ أَفْقَرَ النَّاسَ وَعَلَيْهِ أَثَرُ الضَّرْبِ فِي ظَهْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wālī nasmaʿu kalāma liṣṣin qad afqara al-nāsa wa-ʿalayhi athāru al-ḍarbi fī ẓahrihi
sentences.l: And said the governor: We-hear the-speech of-a-thief who has impoverished the-people, while upon-him (is) the-mark of-the-beating in his-back.
sentences.i: The governor said, "Are we to listen to the words of a thief who has beggared people, with the marks of a beating still on his back?"
sentences.n: نَسْمَعُ is the plain indicative, "we hear", but the sense is a scornful question. The governor takes the brother's earlier lashes (from the judge's men, in the preceding episode) as proof of guilt. The final clause is a circumstantial clause introduced by وَ: "while on him is the mark of the beating".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ مَا فَعَلُوا بِكَ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ إِلَّا عَنْ جُرْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu mā faʿalū bika hādhā al-amra illā ʿan jurmin ʿaẓīmin
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: They-did not do to-you this matter except on-account-of a-crime great.
sentences.i: And he said to him, "They would never have done this to you except for some great crime."
sentences.n: عَنْ here is "on account of, because of".

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ بِضَرْبِ مِائَةِ سَوْطٍ
sentences.tr: fa-amara bi-ḍarbi miʾati sawṭin
sentences.l: And he-ordered the-striking of-a-hundred lashes.
sentences.i: Then he ordered a hundred lashes.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ بِ takes the thing ordered with بِ: "he ordered (the doing of) a beating". سَوْط is a whip or lash, and also the stroke of it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ضُرِبَ أَخِي مِائَةَ سَوْطٍ
sentences.tr: thumma ḍuriba akhī miʾata sawṭin
sentences.l: Then was-struck my-brother a-hundred lashes.
sentences.i: Then my brother was given a hundred lashes.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلُوهُ عَلَى جَمَلٍ وَنَادَوْا عَلَيْهِ هَذَا جَزَاءُ وَأَقَلُّ مِنْ أُجْزِيَ مَنْ يَهْجُمُ بُيُوتَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamalūhu ʿalā jamalin wa-nādaw ʿalayhi hādhā jazāʾu wa-aqallu min ujziya man yahjumu buyūta al-nāsi
sentences.l: Then they-carried-him upon a-camel and cried against-him: This (is) a-recompense, and less than (what) is-recompensed (to) whoever bursts-into houses of-the-people.
sentences.i: Then they mounted him on a camel and proclaimed against him, "This is the reward, and a light one, for whoever bursts into people's houses!"
sentences.n: The wording of the cry is obscure. The print has وَأَقَلُّ مِنْ أُجْزِيَ مَنْ, which looks corrupt; I have pointed it as "and less than is repaid (to) whoever...", taking the stray alif of اجزي as a slip for جُزِيَ ("was repaid"), but a word may have dropped out. The sense is clear: it is a public proclamation of the crime while the offender is paraded. يَهْجُمُ takes its object directly ("bursts into houses"), where Classical would use عَلَى. نَادَى عَلَيْهِ is "to cry (a proclamation) about him".

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ بِإِخْرَاجِهِ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-amara bi-ikhrājihi mina al-madīnati
sentences.l: And he-ordered the-expelling-of-him from the-city.
sentences.i: And he ordered him expelled from the city.

sentences.t: وَهَاجَ أَخِي عَلَى وَجْهِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-hāja akhī ʿalā wajhihi
sentences.l: And surged my-brother upon his-face.
sentences.i: And my brother set off in a daze, wherever his face led him.
sentences.n: هَاجَ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ is the idiom of setting off distraught and aimless, wherever one's face happens to point; the usual form of this idiom is هَامَ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ بِهِ أَنَا خَرَجْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَاسْتَخْبَرْتُهُ فَأَخْبَرَنِي بِحَدِيثِهِ وَمَا جَرَى لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu bihi anā kharajtu ilayhi wa-istakhbartuhu fa-akhbaranī bi-ḥadīthihi wa-mā jarā lahu
sentences.l: And when I-heard of-him, I, I-went-out to-him and questioned-him, and he-informed-me of-his-account and what happened to-him.
sentences.i: When I heard about him, I went out to him and asked for news, and he told me his story and all that had happened to him.
sentences.n: سَمِعَ بِ means "to hear of, to hear about". The separate pronoun أَنَا adds emphasis ("I, for my part").

sentences.t: وَلَا زِلْتُ مَعَهُ دَائِرًا وَهُمْ يُنَادُونَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى سَيَّبُوهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lā ziltu maʿahu dāʾiran wa-hum yunādūna ʿalayhi ḥattā sayyabūhu
sentences.l: And I-did-not-cease with-him going-around, while they crying against-him, until they-let-him-loose.
sentences.i: I kept going about with him while they cried out against him, until they let him go.
sentences.n: وَلَا زِلْتُ for the Classical مَا زِلْتُ ("I did not cease") is a Middle Arabic usage: لَا with a perfect in the sense of "never ceased". سَيَّبَ is "to let loose, to set free", a colloquial-flavoured word the Classical language also knows.

sentences.t: فَأَتَيْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَأَخَذْتُهُ وَأَدْخَلْتُهُ الْمَدِينَةَ سِرًّا وَرَتَّبْتُ لَهُ مَايَأْ كُلُ وَمَا يَشْرَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-ataytu ilayhi wa-akhadhtuhu wa-adkhaltuhu al-madīnata sirran wa-rattabtu lahu mā yaʾkulu wa-mā yashrabu
sentences.l: And I-came to-him and took-him and made-him-enter the-city secretly, and arranged for-him what he-eats and what he-drinks.
sentences.i: I came to him, took him, and brought him back into the city in secret, and arranged for his food and drink.
sentences.n: The print divides ما يأكل wrongly as مايا كل ("mā-yā kul"); I keep the printed division and point it so that it reads mā yaʾkulu. رَتَّبَ لَهُ is "to set aside, to provide for".

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَخِى الْخَامِسُ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ مَقْطُوعَ الْأُذُنَيْنِ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā akhī al-khāmisu fa-innahu kāna maqṭūʿa al-udhunayni yā amīra al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: And as-for my-brother the-fifth, then-indeed-he was cut-off-of the-two-ears, O commander of-the-believers.
sentences.i: As for my fifth brother, O Commander of the Faithful, he was a man with both ears cut off.
sentences.n: Here the tale turns to the next brother, and the speaker addresses the caliph. وَأَمَّا … فَـ is the usual "as for … then" pair, the فَ marking the start of the comment. مَقْطُوعَ الْأُذُنَيْنِ is a half-annexation ("cut-of-the-ears"): "with the ears cut off".

sentences.t: وَكَانَ رَجُلًا فَقِيرًا وَكَانَ يَسْأَلُ النَّاسَ لَيْلًا وَيُنْفِقُ بِهِ نَهَارًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna rajulan faqīran wa-kāna yasʾalu al-nāsa laylan wa-yunfiqu bihi nahāran
sentences.l: And he-was a-man poor, and he-was begging the-people by-night and spending with-it by-day.
sentences.i: He was a poor man, who begged from people at night and spent what he got by day.
sentences.n: يَسْأَلُ النَّاسَ "asks the people" is the idiom for begging. The بِهِ in يُنْفِقُ بِهِ refers back to what he begged: "spent with it", that is "out of it". كَانَ plus the imperfect gives a habitual past.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ وَالِدُنَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ طَاعِنٌ فِى السِّنِّ فَاعْتَلَّ وَمَاتَ فَخَلَّفَ لَنَا سَبْعَمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna wālidunā shaykhun kabīrun ṭāʿinun fī al-sinni fa-iʿtalla wa-māta fa-khallafa lanā sabʿamiʾati dirhamin
sentences.l: And was our-father an-old-man, great, advanced in the-age; then he-fell-ill and died, and left to-us seven-hundred dirhams.
sentences.i: Our father was a very old man, far gone in years; he fell ill and died, and left us seven hundred dirhams.
sentences.n: Middle Arabic: after كَانَ the predicate stays in the nominative, شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ طَاعِنٌ, where Classical would have the accusative (شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا طَاعِنًا). I point what the text says. طَعَنَ فِى السِّنِّ is "to be advanced in years" (literally "to pierce into age"). The numeral is in the print one word, سبعمائة, "seven hundred".

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَّا مِائَةَ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha kullu wāḥidin minnā miʾata dirhamin
sentences.l: So took each one of-us a-hundred dirhams.
sentences.i: Each of us took a hundred dirhams.
sentences.n: Seven hundred dirhams among seven brothers gives a hundred each.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَخِي الْخَامِسُ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا أَخَذَ حِصَّتَهُ تَحَيَّرَ وَلَمْ يَدْرِ مَا يَصْنَعُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā akhī al-khāmisu fa-innahu lammā akhadha ḥiṣṣatahu taḥayyara wa-lam yadri mā yaṣnaʿu bihā
sentences.l: And as-for my-brother the-fifth, then-indeed-he, when he-took his-share, was-bewildered and did-not know what he-should-do with-it.
sentences.i: As for my fifth brother, when he took his share he was bewildered and did not know what to do with it.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ وَقَعَ فِى خَاطِرِهِ أَنَّهُ يَأْخُذُ بِهَا زُجَاجًا مِنْ كُلِّ نَوْعٍ وَيَنْتَفِعُ بِثَمَنِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa ka-dhālika idh waqaʿa fī khāṭirihi annahu yaʾkhudhu bihā zujājan min kulli nawʿin wa-yantafiʿu bi-thamanihi
sentences.l: And while he (was) thus, behold, there-fell in his-mind that-he take with-it glass of every kind and benefit by-its-price.
sentences.i: While he was in this state, the thought came to him that he would buy glassware of every kind with it, and profit from its price.
sentences.n: بَيْنَمَا … إِذْ is the "while … suddenly" frame. خَاطِر is "mind, what passes through the mind"; وَقَعَ فِى خَاطِرِهِ is "it occurred to him". أَخَذَ بِ here means "to take (something) with, to buy with" (the money). زُجَاج is glass, here glass vessels.

sentences.t: فَاشْتَرَى بِالْمِائَةِ الدِّرْهَمِ زُجَاجًا وَجَعَلَهُ فِى طَبَقٍ كَبِيرٍ وَقَعَدَ فِى مَوْضِعٍ يَبِيعُ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ishtarā bi-al-miʾati al-dirhami zujājan wa-jaʿalahu fī ṭabaqin kabīrin wa-qaʿada fī mawḍiʿin yabīʿu fīhi
sentences.l: And he-bought with-the-hundred the-dirham glass, and put-it in a-tray large, and sat in a-place (where) he-sells in-it.
sentences.i: He bought glass with the hundred dirhams, put it in a large tray, and sat down in a place where he sold his wares.
sentences.n: بِالْمِائَةِ الدِّرْهَمِ puts the noun after the numeral with the article on both ("the hundred the dirham"), a Middle Arabic way of saying "the hundred dirhams"; Classical would say بِالْمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ or بِمِائَةِ الدِّرْهَمِ. اشْتَرَى بِ is "to buy with (a price)". The tray holds his stock, as in the next sentences.

sentences.t: وَبِجَانِبِهِ حَائِطٌ فَأَسْنَدَ ظَهْرَهُ إِلَيْهِ وَقَعَدَ مُتَفَكِّرًا فِى نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-bi-jānibihi ḥāʾiṭun fa-asnada ẓahrahu ilayhi wa-qaʿada mutafakkiran fī nafsihi
sentences.l: And at-his-side (was) a-wall, so he-leaned his-back to-it and sat thinking in himself.
sentences.i: Beside him was a wall, so he leaned his back against it and sat musing to himself.
sentences.n: بِجَانِبِهِ is "at his side" (بِ marks place: "by, at"). فِى نَفْسِهِ is "in himself, privately".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ إِنَّ رَأْسَ مَالِي فِي هَذَا الزُّجَاجِ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ وَأَنَا أَبِيعُهُ بِمِائَتَيْنِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla inna raʾsa mālī fī hādhā al-zujāji miʾatu dirhamin wa-anā abīʿuhu bi-miʾatayni dirhamin
sentences.l: And he-said: Indeed the-head of-my-wealth in this glass (is) a-hundred dirhams, and I, I-sell-it for-two-hundred dirhams,
sentences.i: And he said to himself, "My capital in this glass is a hundred dirhams, and I shall sell it for two hundred dirhams;
sentences.n: رَأْسُ الْمَالِ is the capital ("head of the wealth"). Here and below the counted noun after the hundreds is singular (دِرْهَمٍ), as the print has it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَشْتَرِي بِمِائَتَيْنِ دِرْهَمٍ زُجَاجًا وَأَبِيعُهُ بِأَرْبَعِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: thumma ashtarī bi-miʾatayni dirhamin zujājan wa-abīʿuhu bi-arbaʿimiʾati dirhamin
sentences.l: Then I-buy for-two-hundred dirhams glass and sell-it for-four-hundred dirhams,
sentences.i: then I shall buy glass with two hundred dirhams and sell it for four hundred,
sentences.n: The speaker uses the present tense for what he plans ("I sell, I buy"). Note the repeated اشترى بِ: "buy with (a price)".

sentences.t: وَلَا أَزَالُ أَبِيعُ وَأَشْتَرِي إِلَى أَنْ يَبْقَى مَعِي مَالٌ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-lā azālu abīʿu wa-ashtarī ilā an yabqā maʿī mālun kathīrun
sentences.l: And I-do-not cease selling and buying until remains with-me wealth much.
sentences.i: And I shall keep buying and selling until I have a great deal of money left.
sentences.n: لَا أَزَالُ with an imperfect is "I shall not cease to"; the following verbs have no conjunction, as in Classical ("I do not cease: I sell, I buy").

sentences.t: فَأَشْتَرِيَ بِهِ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْمَتْجَرِ وَ الْجَوَاهِرِ وَالْعَطْرِفَأَرْبَحَ رِبْحًا عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: fa-ashtariya bihi min jamīʿi al-matjari wa-al-jawāhiri wa-al-ʿaṭri fa-arbaḥa ribḥan ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: Then I-buy with-it of all the-merchandise and the-jewels and the-perfume, and so-I-profit a-profit great.
sentences.i: Then I shall buy with it every sort of merchandise, jewels and perfumes, and make a huge profit.
sentences.n: The print has two oddities: a stray space in المتجر و الجواهر ("the merchandise and the jewels"), and the last words run together as والعطرفاربح, which I split as وَالْعَطْرِ + فَأَرْبَحَ but keep unspaced as printed. الْمَتْجَر is "trade, merchandise". The subjunctives أَشْتَرِيَ and أَرْبَحَ follow فَ of consequence after the "until" clause. رِبْحًا is a cognate accusative.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَشْتَرِي دَارًا حَسَنَةً وَأَشْتَرِي الْمَمَالِيكَ وَالْخَيْلَ وَسُرُوجَ الذَّهَبِ وَآكُلُ وَأَشْرَبُ وَلَا أُخَلِّي مُغَنِّيًا وَلَا مُغَنِّيَةً فِى الْمَدِينَةِ حَتَّى أَجِيبَهَا عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda dhālika ashtarī dāran ḥasanatan wa-ashtarī al-mamālīka wa-al-khayla wa-surūja al-dhahabi wa-ākulu wa-ashrabu wa-lā ukhallī mughanniyan wa-lā mughanniyatan fī al-madīnati ḥattā ajībahā ʿindī
sentences.l: And after that I-buy a-house beautiful, and I-buy the-mamluks and the-horses and saddles of-gold, and I-eat and I-drink, and do-not I-leave a-singer-man or a-singer-woman in the-city until I-bring-her to-me.
sentences.i: After that I shall buy a fine house, and buy mamluks and horses and saddles of gold, and I shall eat and drink, and leave no singer, man or woman, in the city, until I have brought her to my house.
sentences.n: In the print وَأَكُلُ is spelled with a single alif, and is read wa-ākulu (wa-aʾkulu, "and I eat"), so I point it with madda. الْمَمَالِيك are "slaves", specifically owned slaves, pl. of مَمْلُوك. أَجِيبَهَا is "I bring her" (جَابَ, a colloquial form of جَاءَ بِ, "to bring"). The singular feminine "her" refers back to the female singer (مُغَنِّيَة), the only one he means to fetch; the masculine mughanniyan "singer" is named first for completeness.

sentences.t: وَأَعْمَلُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى رَأْسَ مَالِي مِائَةَ أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿmalu in shāʾa Allāhu taʿālā raʾsa mālī miʾata alfi dirhamin
sentences.l: And I-make, if willed God (be) exalted, my-capital a-hundred thousand dirhams.
sentences.i: And, God willing, I shall make my capital a hundred thousand dirhams.
sentences.n: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ("if God, may He be exalted, wills") is the usual pious tag on a plan for the future. عَمِلَ with two objects means "to make (something) into (something)".

sentences.t: هَذَا كُلُّهُ هُوَ يَحْسُبُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَقَفَصُ الزُّجَاجِ مَطْرُوحٌ قُدَّامَهُ
sentences.tr: hādhā kulluhu huwa yaḥsubu fī nafsihi wa-qafaṣu al-zujāji maṭrūḥun quddāmahu
sentences.l: This all-of-it, he (was) reckoning in himself, and the-crate of-the-glass (was) thrown before-him.
sentences.i: All this he reckoned to himself, while the crate of glass lay on the ground in front of him.
sentences.n: Narrator's voice. قَفَص is a crate or cage; the earlier sentence called the container a طَبَق ("tray"), so the vessel has changed names between lines. مَطْرُوح ("thrown down, set down") and the colloquial قُدَّام ("in front of", for Classical أَمَام) are plain-style words.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ وَإِذَا صَارَ مَالِي مِائَةَ أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ أَبْعَثُ الدَّلَّالَاتِ فِي خِطْبَةِ بَنَاتِ الْمُلُوكِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla wa-idhā ṣāra mālī miʾata alfi dirhamin abʿathu al-dallālāti fī khiṭbati banāti al-mulūki wa-al-wuzarāʾi
sentences.l: Then he-said: And when became my-wealth a-hundred thousand dirhams, I-send the-brokeresses for the-betrothal-seeking of-daughters of-the-kings and the-viziers,
sentences.i: Then he said, "And when my money has become a hundred thousand dirhams, I shall send the matchmaking women to ask for the daughters of kings and viziers,
sentences.n: الدَّلَّالَات are the women who go between households as brokers (and sell things door to door), here acting as matchmakers; the singular is دَلَّالَة. خِطْبَة is the asking for a woman in marriage, and فِى here means "in the matter of".

sentences.t: وَأَخْطُبُ بِنْتَ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhṭubu binta al-wazīri
sentences.l: and I-ask-in-marriage the-daughter of-the-vizier,
sentences.i: and I shall ask for the vizier's daughter in marriage,

sentences.t: فَقَدْ
sentences.tr: fa-qad
sentences.l: for indeed
sentences.i: for indeed
sentences.n: The slice ends here; the sentence continues in the next lines of print. فَقَدْ introduces a reason: "for indeed (I have heard that…)".

sentences.t: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهَا كَامِلَةٌ فِى أَحْسَنِ بَدِيعَةٍ فِى الْجَمَالِ
sentences.tr: balaghanī annahā kāmilatun fī aḥsani badīʿatin fī al-jamāli
sentences.l: It-reached me that-she (is) perfect, in the best marvel, in beauty,
sentences.i: I have heard that she is flawless, the loveliest marvel of beauty,
sentences.n: The speech begins in the middle of a sentence. فِى is printed with an undotted ى, while بَلَغَنِي has a dotted ي; both are kept as printed. بَدِيعَة is a wonder, a thing of marvellous making.

sentences.t: وَأُمْهِرُهَا بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-umhiruhā bi-alfi dīnārin
sentences.l: and-I-give-her-a-dowry with a-thousand dinar,
sentences.i: and I will pay her a dowry of a thousand dinars.
sentences.n: The imperfect carries a future sense, as a plan: "I will give her a dowry". The dowry (مَهْر) is paid by the groom.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ رَضِيَ أَبُوهَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-in raḍiya abūhā kāna
sentences.l: And if consented her-father, it-was.
sentences.i: If her father consents, well and good;
sentences.n: كَانَ stands alone for "so it is, so be it": the perfect of the apodosis speaks of a thing as already settled.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ يَرْضَ أَخَذْتُهَا قَهْرًا عَنْ رَغْمِ أَنْفِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam yarḍa akhadhtuhā qahran ʿan raghmi anfihi
sentences.l: and if not he-consents, I-took-her by-force, from the rubbing-in-the-dust of his-nose.
sentences.i: and if he refuses, I will take her by force, in spite of him.
sentences.n: Again a perfect (أَخَذْتُهَا) after "if", with future meaning. عَنْ رَغْمِ أَنْفِهِ is a fixed idiom: his nose rubbed in the dust, that is, over his dead body, whether he likes it or not.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ حَصَلَتْ فِي دَارِي
sentences.tr: fa-in ḥaṣalat fī dārī
sentences.l: And if she-was-obtained in my-house,
sentences.i: Once she is in my house,

sentences.t: أَشْتَرِي عَشَرَةَ خُدَّامٍ صِغَارٍ
sentences.tr: ashtarī ʿasharata khuddāmin ṣighārin
sentences.l: I-buy ten servants, small-ones;
sentences.i: I will buy ten young servants,
sentences.n: The apodosis of the long daydream begins here without any connecting particle, a plain imperfect. خُدَّام is a plural of خَادِم, "servant".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَشْتَرِي لِي كِسْوَةً مِنْ كَسَاوِي الْمُلُوكِ وَالسَّلَاطِينِ
sentences.tr: thumma ashtarī lī kiswatan min kasāwī al-mulūki wa-al-salāṭīni
sentences.l: then I-buy for-me a-robe from the-robes of-the-kings and-the-sultans;
sentences.i: then I will buy myself a robe of the kind that kings and sultans wear,

sentences.t: وَأَصْنَعُ لِي سَرْجَ ذَهَبٍ وَأُرَصِّعُهُ بِالْجَوَاهِرِ الْمُثَمَّنَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-aṣnaʿu lī sarja dhahabin wa-uraṣṣiʿuhu bi-al-jawāhiri al-muthamanati
sentences.l: and-I-make for-me a-saddle of-gold, and-I-inlay-it with-the-jewels, the-valued-ones;
sentences.i: and I will have a golden saddle made for me and inlay it with costly jewels;
sentences.n: الْمُثَمَّنَة, "priced, valuable", is the passive participle of ثَمَّنَ "to value": jewels of great price.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرْكَبُ وَمَعِى الْمَمَالِيكُ يَمْشُونَ حَوْلِي وَقُدَّ امِي
sentences.tr: thumma arkabu wa-maʿī al-mamālīku yamshūna ḥawlī wa-quddāmī
sentences.l: then I-ride, and with-me the-mamluks walk around-me and in-front-of-me;
sentences.i: then I will ride out with my mamluks walking all around me and before me;
sentences.n: The print breaks وَقُدَّامِي ("and in front of me") into two words, وقد امي. We keep the break and point the pieces so they read as one word. المماليك are slave-soldiers, here the young servants bought just above.

sentences.t: وَأَدُورُ الْمَدِينَةَ وَالنَّاسُ يُسَلِّمُونَ عَلَيَّ وَيَدْعُونَ لِي
sentences.tr: wa-adūru al-madīnata wa-al-nāsu yusallimūna ʿalayya wa-yadʿūna lī
sentences.l: and-I-go-around the-city, and-the-people greet upon-me and-pray for-me;
sentences.i: and I will make the rounds of the city while the people greet me and pray for me;

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ الَّذِي هُوَ أَبُوالْبِنْتِ
sentences.tr: thumma adkhulu ʿalā al-wazīri al-ladhī huwa abū al-bint
sentences.l: then I-enter upon the-vizier, who he (is) the-father-of-the-girl,
sentences.i: then I will go in to the vizier, the girl's father,
sentences.n: أَبُوالْبِنْتِ is printed as a single word, "father-of-the-girl". دَخَلَ عَلَى is the usual idiom for entering into someone's presence.

sentences.t: وَالْمَمَالِيكُ خَلْفِي وَقُدَّامِي وَعَنْ يَمِينِي وَعَنْ شِمَالِي
sentences.tr: wa-al-mamālīku khalfī wa-quddāmī wa-ʿan yamīnī wa-ʿan shimālī
sentences.l: and-the-mamluks behind-me and in-front-of-me and from my-right and from my-left;
sentences.i: with the mamluks behind me and before me, on my right and on my left;

sentences.t: فَإِذَا رَآنِي قَامَ الْوَزِيرُإِلَيَّ قَائِمًا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā raʾānī qāma al-wazīru ilayya qāʾiman
sentences.l: and-when he-sees-me, rises the-vizier to-me, standing,
sentences.i: and when he sees me, the vizier will rise and come to me, standing,
sentences.n: The print runs الوزير and إلي together; we keep it as one written word. The edition's own precomposed آ in رَآنِي and ئ in قَائِمًا are kept. "Rises, standing" is a pleonasm of the spoken language.

sentences.t: وَأَقْعَدَنِي مَكَانَهُ وَيَقْعُدُ هُوَ دُونِي لِأَنَّهُ صِهْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-aqʿadanī makānahu wa-yaqʿudu huwa dūnī li-annahu ṣihrī
sentences.l: and-he-seats-me in-his-place, and he-sits, he, below-me, because-he (is) my-in-law;
sentences.i: and seat me in his own place and sit below me himself, since he is to be my in-law by marriage,
sentences.n: صِهْر covers any relation by marriage; here it is the man who will be the speaker's father-in-law. The perfect وَأَقْعَدَنِي runs on in the same future-minded sequence as the imperfects around it.

sentences.t: وَيَكُونُ مَعِي خَادِمَيْنِ بِكِيسَيْنِ فِي كُلِّ كِيسٍ أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-yakūnu maʿī khādimayni bi-kīsayni fī kulli kīsin alfu dīnārin
sentences.l: and there-will-be with-me two-servants with-two-purses, in every purse a-thousand dinar,
sentences.i: and with me will be two servants carrying two purses, a thousand dinars in each,
sentences.n: خَادِمَيْنِ is the oblique dual where Classical would have the nominative خَادِمَانِ as subject of يَكُونُ; Middle Arabic often uses the oblique dual everywhere. Printed so, and pointed so. The بِـ of بِكِيسَيْنِ means "carrying, with".

sentences.t: فَأُعْطِيهِ الْأَلْفَ مَهْرَ بِنْةِ
sentences.tr: fa-uʿṭīhi al-alfa mahra binti
sentences.l: so I-give-him the-thousand, the-dowry-of the-girl,
sentences.i: I will hand him the one thousand as the girl's dowry
sentences.n: The print has بنة with a tāʾ marbūṭa where بنت ("daughter, girl") or perhaps بنته ("his daughter") is meant. We point only the letters present, read as bint. The sense is the same either way.

sentences.t: وَأُهْدِي لَهُ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ أُخْرَى حَتَّى يَعْلَمَ مُرُوَّتِي وَكَرَمِي وَكِبَرَ نَفْسِي وَصِغَرَ الدُّنْيَا فِي عَيْنِي
sentences.tr: wa-uhdī lahu alfa dīnārin ukhrā ḥattā yaʿlama muruwwatī wa-karamī wa-kibara nafsī wa-ṣighara al-dunyā fī ʿaynī
sentences.l: and-I-gift to-him a-thousand dinar another, until he-knows my-manliness and-my-generosity and-the-greatness of-my-soul and-the-smallness of-the-world in my-eye;
sentences.i: and give him another thousand dinars as a gift, so that he may know my manliness and my generosity, the greatness of my spirit, and how small the world is in my eyes;
sentences.n: مُرُوَّتِي is printed مروتي, without the hamza of the fuller spelling مروءة; it means manly virtue, honour, magnanimity. كِبَر نَفْسِي, "greatness of soul", is lofty pride in the good sense.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا خَاطَبَنِي بِعَشْرِ كَلِمَاتٍ أَجَبْتُهُ بِكَلِمَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā khāṭabanī bi-ʿashri kalimātin ajabtuhu bi-kalimatayni
sentences.l: and-when he-addresses-me with ten words, I-answer-him with two words;
sentences.i: and when he addresses me in ten words, I will answer him in two;
sentences.n: Perfects after إِذَا stand for habitual future action: "whenever he speaks, I answer".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْصَرِفُ إِلَى دَارِي
sentences.tr: thumma anṣarifu ilā dārī
sentences.l: then I-depart to my-house.
sentences.i: Then I will go back to my house.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ جِهَةِ امْرَأَتِي وَهَبْتُ لَهُ دَرَاهِمَ وَخَلَعْتُ عَلَيْهِ خِلْعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-idhā jāʾa aḥadun min jihati imraʾatī wahabtu lahu darāhima wa-khalaʿtu ʿalayhi khilʿatan
sentences.l: And-when comes anyone from the-side of-my-wife, I-gave to-him dirhams and-I-bestowed upon-him a-robe-of-honour;
sentences.i: And when anyone comes from my wife's side, I will give him money and bestow a robe of honour on him;
sentences.n: جِهَة, "side", here means "quarter, family". خَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ خِلْعَةً is to confer a robe of honour, the courtly reward. The perfects here (وَهَبْتُ, وَخَلَعْتُ) keep the daydream's future sense. The edition prints امرأتي with a precomposed أ; it is kept.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ جَاءَنِي بِهَدِيَّةٍ رَدَّيْتُهَا عَلَيْهِ وَلَمْ أَقْبَلْهَا مِنْهُ حَتَّى يَعْلَمُوا أَنِّي عَزِيزُ النَّفْسِ
sentences.tr: wa-in jāʾanī bi-hadiyyatin raddaytuhā ʿalayhi wa-lam aqbalhā minhu ḥattā yaʿlamū annī ʿazīzu al-nafsi
sentences.l: and-if he-comes-to-me with-a-gift, I-returned-it upon-him and-did-not accept-it from-him, until they-know that-I (am) dear-of-soul;
sentences.i: and if he brings me a gift, I will send it back to him and not accept it, so that they will know I am a man of proud spirit;
sentences.n: رَدَّيْتُهَا is a spoken-style form (from رَدَّى), where Classical has رَدَدْتُهَا. عَزِيزُ النَّفْسِ, "dear of soul", means self-respecting, not to be bought. The بِـ of بِهَدِيَّةٍ marks what he comes with.

sentences.t: وَلَا أُخَلِّي نَفْسِي إِلَّا فِي مَوْضِعِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lā ukhallī nafsī illā fī mawḍiʿihā
sentences.l: and I-do-not leave myself except in its-place;
sentences.i: and that I put myself nowhere but in my proper place;
sentences.n: أُخَلِّي نَفْسِي, "I leave myself", is "I set myself", "I let myself be". The clause still depends on the "until they know" that precedes it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أُقَدِّمُ إِلَيْهِمْ بِإِ صْلَاحِ شَأْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma uqaddimu ilayhim bi-iṣlāḥi shaʾnī
sentences.l: then I-present to-them with the-setting-right of-my-affair;
sentences.i: then I will turn to them and put my affair in order;
sentences.n: The print has a space inside بإصلاح (با صلاح). We keep the break and point the first piece بِإِ and the second صْلَاحِ so that together they read bi-iṣlāḥi. The sense of أُقَدِّمُ إِلَيْهِمْ بِـ is a little loose: "I come forward to them with ...".

sentences.t: فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ أَمَرْتُهُمْ بِزِفَا فِيهَا وَأُصْلِحُ دَارِي إِصْلَاحًا بَيِّنًا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā faʿalū dhālika amartuhum bi-zifā fīhā wa-uṣliḥu dārī iṣlāḥan bayyinan
sentences.l: And-when they-do that, I-command-them with zifā(?) (perhaps zifāfihā, "her bridal procession") in-her, and-I-put-right my-house, a-putting-right clear;
sentences.i: And when they have done that, I will order them to bring her in procession, and I will put my house in handsome order;
sentences.n: بِزِفَا فِيهَا is obscure. It looks like a damaged بزفافها ("with her bridal procession", from زِفَاف, the leading of the bride to her husband), or a stray فيها after a shortened زفا. I translate the sense and give the letters as printed. أَمَرَ بِـ is the verb's own preposition: "command to do". إِصْلَاحًا بَيِّنًا is a cognate accusative, "a clear, evident putting-right".

sentences.t: فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَقْتُ الْجِلَاءِ لَبِسْتُ أَفْخَرَ ثِيَابِي
sentences.tr: fa-idhā jāʾa waqtu al-jilāʾi labistu afkhara thiyābī
sentences.l: And-when comes the-time of-the-unveiling, I-wore the-most-splendid of-my-clothes
sentences.i: And when the time of the unveiling comes, I will put on my finest clothes
sentences.n: الْجِلَاء here is the "displaying" of the bride to the groom (usually جِلْوَة); the edition's ء is kept. لَبِسْتُ is a perfect again in the future-minded series.

sentences.t: وَقَعَدْتُ فِي بَدْلَةٍ مِنَ الدِّيبَاجِ مُتَّكِئًا لَا أَلْتَفِتُ يَمِينًا وَلَا شِمَالًا لِكِبَرِ عَقْلِي وَرَزَانَةِ فَهْمِي
sentences.tr: wa-qaʿadtu fī badlatin mina al-dībāji muttakiʾan lā altafitu yamīnan wa-lā shimālan li-kibari ʿaqlī wa-razānati fahmī
sentences.l: and-I-sat in a-suit of-the-brocade, reclining, I-do-not turn right and-not left, for-the-greatness of-my-mind and-the-gravity of-my-understanding;
sentences.i: and sit in a suit of brocade, reclining, turning neither right nor left, so great is my mind and so weighty my understanding;
sentences.n: بَدْلَة is a suit or set of clothes. The edition prints مُتَّكِئًا with a precomposed ئ; it is kept. The لِـ of لِكِبَرِ gives the reason: "because of, out of". رَزَانَة is steadiness, gravity.

sentences.t: وَتَكُونُ امْرَأَتِي قَائِمَةً قَدْ أَمْسَى كَالْبَدْرِ وَهِى فِي حُلِيِّهَا وَحُلَلِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-takūnu imraʾatī qāʾimatan qad amsā ka-al-badri wa-hiya fī ḥuliyyihā wa-ḥulalihā
sentences.l: and my-wife will-be standing, he-had-become like-the-full-moon, and she in her-jewels and-her-robes,
sentences.i: while my wife stands there, grown radiant as the full moon, in her jewels and her robes,
sentences.n: قَدْ أَمْسَى is masculine where the wife calls for أَمْسَتْ ("she has become"). It may be a slip, or أَمْسَى may be the impersonal "evening came"; the sense "she has become like the full moon" is the likelier. كَالْبَدْرِ: كَـ is "like". حُلَل are robes (pl. of حُلَّة), حُلِيّ ornaments.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا عُجْبًا وَتِيهًـا
sentences.tr: wa-anā anẓuru ilayhā ʿujban wa-tīhan
sentences.l: and I look at-her in-vanity and-in-pride,
sentences.i: and I look at her with vain delight and pride
sentences.n: The edition puts a damma on عُجْبًا and a lengthening stroke (ـ) in وَتِيهًـا; both are kept in place. عُجْب is self-admiration, conceit, and تِيه haughtiness; the two accusatives say how he looks.

sentences.t: حَتَّى يَقُولَ جَمِيعُ مَنْ حَضَرَنَا سَيِّدِي امْرَأَنُكَ وَجَارِيَتُكَ قَائِمَةٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ فَأَنْعِمْ عَلَيْهَا بِالنَّظَرِ فَقَدْ أَضَرَّبِهَا الْقِيَامُ
sentences.tr: ḥattā yaqūla jamīʿu man ḥaḍaranā sayyidī imraʾatuka wa-jāriyatuka qāʾimatun bayna yadayka fa-anʿim ʿalayhā bi-al-naẓari fa-qad aḍarra bihā al-qiyāmu
sentences.l: until says all of-those-who attended-us: My-lord, your-wife and-your-slave-girl (is) standing between your-hands, so grant favour upon-her with-the-look, for harmed her the-standing.
sentences.i: until everyone present says, "My lord, your wife and your slave girl stands before you; do her the kindness of a glance, for standing so long has worn her out."
sentences.n: The print has امراتك with a nūn in place of the tā': امرانك. We point the letters as printed, for the sense imraʾatuka, "your wife". The edition also prints a shadda in اضرّبها, that is أَضَرَّ بِهَا ("it has harmed her"), joined in one word; it is kept in place. أَنْعِمْ عَلَيْهَا بِـ, "favour her with"; the بِـ names the favour: a look. The feminine singular قَائِمَةٌ agrees with the nearer subject, جَارِيَتُكَ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ يَبُوسُونَ الْأَرْضَ قُدَّامِي مِرَارًا
sentences.tr: thumma yabūsūna al-arḍa quddāmī mirāran
sentences.l: then they-kiss the-ground in-front-of-me, many-times;
sentences.i: Then they kiss the ground before me again and again,
sentences.n: بَاسَ يَبُوسُ, "to kiss", is the everyday word, commoner in speech than the Classical قَبَّلَ. Kissing the ground is the courtly gesture of homage.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَرْفَعُ رَأْسِي وَأَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا نَظْرَةًوَاحِدَةً
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika arfaʿu raʾsī wa-anẓuru ilayhā naẓratan wāḥidatan
sentences.l: and at that, I-raise my-head and-I-look at-her one-look,
sentences.i: and at that I lift my head and give her a single look,
sentences.n: نَظْرَةًوَاحِدَةً is printed as one word, "a look, one". Because of the glued spelling, the tanwīn is written on the ة.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أُطْرِقُ بِرَأْسِي إِلَى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: thumma uṭriqu bi-raʾsī ilā al-arḍi
sentences.l: then I-lower with-my-head to the-ground;
sentences.i: then I bow my head to the ground;
sentences.n: أَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ is "to lower one's head"; the بِـ here simply attaches the head as what is lowered.

sentences.t: فَيَمْضُونَ بِهَا إِلَى مَجْلِسِ امَنَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-yamḍūna bihā ilā majlisi al-manāmi
sentences.l: and-they-go with-her to the-sitting-place of-the-sleep(?),
sentences.i: and they take her away to the bedchamber;
sentences.n: امنام is probably المنام with the lām dropped by the printer ("the sleeping place", with مجلس "sitting place" in the sense of room). The tr gives the article with the lām restored. مَضَى بِـ is "to go off with, take away".

sentences.t: وَأَقُومُ أَنَا وَأُغَيِّرُ قُمَاشِي وَأَلْبَسُ أَحْسَنَ مِمَّا كَانَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-aqūmu anā wa-ughayyiru qumāshī wa-albasu aḥsana mimmā kāna ʿalayya
sentences.l: and-I-rise, I, and-I-change my-clothes and-I-wear better from-what was upon-me;
sentences.i: while I get up myself, change my clothes, and put on something finer than what I wore before;
sentences.n: قُمَاش is cloth, hence "clothes" in the spoken language. مِمَّا is مِنْ + مَا: "than what".

sentences.t: فَإِذَا جَاؤُا بِالْعَرُوسَةِ الْمَرَّةَ الثَّانِيَةَ لَا أَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا حَتَّى يَسْأَلُونِي مِرَارًا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā jāʾū bi-al-ʿarūsati al-marrata al-thāniyata lā anẓuru ilayhā ḥattā yasʾalūnī mirāran
sentences.l: And-when they-come with-the-bride the-time the-second, I-do-not look at-her until they-ask-me many-times,
sentences.i: And when they bring in the bride a second time, I will not look at her until they have asked me again and again,
sentences.n: جَاؤُا is the edition's own spelling, with a final alif after the wāw and its precomposed ؤ; kept. جَاءَ بِـ is "to bring" (come with). الْمَرَّةَ الثَّانِيَةَ is an accusative of time, "a second time".

sentences.t: وَأَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا ثُمَّ أُطْرِقُ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ وَلَمْ أَزَلْ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ جِلَاؤُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-anẓuru ilayhā thumma uṭriqu ilā al-arḍi wa-lam azal kadhālika ḥattā yatimma jilāʾuhā
sentences.l: and-I-look at-her, then I-lower to the-ground, and I-do-not cease thus until completes her-unveiling.
sentences.i: and then I look at her and lower my eyes to the ground once more, and so I remain until her unveiling is complete.
sentences.n: The edition's ؤ in جِلَاؤُهَا is kept. لَمْ أَزَلْ كَذَلِكَ, "I did not cease thus", means "I keep on like that". In the English the "lowering of the eyes" is read off the verb: أَطْرَقَ is to cast the eyes or head down.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And overtook Shahr Zad the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech, the-permitted.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, ceasing the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula of the night. The print divides her name into two words, شهر زاد, and they are pointed and transliterated as printed (Shahr Zād). الْمُبَاح, "permitted", rhymes with الصَّبَاحُ: this is sajʿ.
